source.name: Lower Dolpa Trek – 19 days
source.summary:
The Lower Dolpa Trek is an extraordinary adventure that delves into one of Nepal’s most remote and untouched regions. Situated in the far-western part of Nepal, this trek offers a rare opportunity to explore an isolated area renowned for its stunning landscapes and unique cultural heritage. The trek provides a fascinating blend of dramatic scenery, high-altitude terrain, and traditional Tibetan-influenced communities.

The journey typically begins with a flight from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, followed by another flight or a lengthy drive to Juphal, the starting point of the trek. From Juphal, you’ll begin your trek, winding through charming villages, terraced fields, and lush green forests. This initial part of the trek offers a gentle introduction to the region’s natural beauty.

One of the key highlights of the Lower Dolpa Trek is the exploration of Shey Phoksundo National Park. The park is home to Shey Phoksundo Lake, Nepal’s largest lake, known for its striking turquoise color and serene setting. The lake, set against a backdrop of snow-capped peaks and steep cliffs, creates a breathtaking vista. A visit to the lake also includes exploring the surrounding areas, such as the impressive Phoksundo Waterfall, one of the highest in Nepal.

As the trek progresses, you’ll traverse a diverse range of landscapes. The lower elevations feature verdant valleys and terraced farmland, while higher altitudes present arid, desert-like environments. This contrast between lush and barren landscapes adds to the trek’s visual and experiential diversity.

The Lower Dolpa region is also rich in cultural heritage. The trek takes you through traditional Tibetan-influenced villages where local customs and lifestyles have remained largely unchanged. The architecture, monasteries, and daily activities reflect a unique blend of Tibetan and Nepali cultures. Engaging with the local communities offers valuable insights into their traditional practices and way of life.

The trek involves navigating challenging terrain, including steep ascents and descents, as well as high-altitude passes. Proper acclimatization is crucial to cope with the demands of the trek. Despite these challenges, the rewards are significant, with spectacular views and a profound sense of achievement.

Typically lasting around 15 to 20 days, the Lower Dolpa Trek provides ample time to explore the region thoroughly. The relatively long duration allows trekkers to fully appreciate the beauty of the landscapes and the richness of the cultural experiences.

Overall, the Lower Dolpa Trek is a remarkable adventure for those seeking a remote and immersive trekking experience. Its combination of stunning natural beauty, diverse landscapes, and rich cultural encounters makes it an unforgettable journey through one of Nepal’s most secluded regions. Whether you’re drawn to the allure of Shey Phoksundo Lake, the challenge of high-altitude trekking, or the chance to experience traditional Tibetan culture, the Lower Dolpa Trek offers an exceptional and memorable adventure in the heart of the Himalayas.
highlights:
Trek along the scenic Bheri River corridor, passing charming villages, terraced fields, gorges, and suspension bridges
Explore Tarakot — an ancient fortress village with deep historical roots as a strategic stronghold
Trek through forested trails of wild roses and juniper bushes to reach Dho Tarap — a historic trade hub between Tibet and the Mustang Kingdom
Acclimatization day in Dho Tarap (4,050m) — essential preparation before tackling two high-altitude passes above 5,000m
Cross the mighty Numa La Pass (5,180m) — with breathtaking panoramic views of Mt. Dhaulagiri and the Churen Himal ranges
Cross the second challenging Baga La Pass (5,170m) — rewarded with sweeping Himalayan vistas and a first glimpse of the stunning Phoksundo Lake below
Arrive at Ringmo village, home to the rare and endangered Bon religion — one of Nepal's most unique and ancient spiritual traditions
Marvel at the legendary Shey Phoksundo Lake (3,730m) — Nepal's largest lake, famous for its mesmerizing deep turquoise color, towering cliffs, and snow-capped backdrop
Dedicated rest and exploration day at Phoksundo Lake — discover the Phoksundo Waterfall, one of Nepal's highest, and immerse in Bon culture
Fully tented camp experience throughout the entire trek — a true wilderness expedition
A contingency day in Kathmandu built in to protect against weather-dependent mountain flight disruptions
A comprehensive 19-day itinerary — ideal for seasoned trekkers seeking an extreme, culturally rich, and deeply rewarding Himalayan adventure
source.itineraries:
Day 1: ARRIVAL IN KATHMANDU
At an arrival at the international airport we will be picked up and then transferred to the hotel. Check in at the hotel and stay overnight.

Day 2: FLY KATHMANDU TO NEPALGUNJ [ 1 HRS; / 150 METERS, 492 FT]
Set off from Kathmandu in the early morning to catch the flight to Nepalgunj. After an hour long flight to Nepalgunj and upon arrival at Nepalgunj airport you will be received by the trekking crew and be transferred to Hotel Batika in Nepalgunj. The overnight stay will be at hotel Batika in Nepalgunj. We can spend some time in the city of Nepalgunj exploring the city and the local markets and shops.

Day 3: FLY NEPALGUNJ TO JUPHAL & TREK TO DUNAI [35 MINS - FLIGHT, 3-4 HRS. / 2150 METERS, 7053 FT.]
Fly to Juphal for about 35 minutes in a STOL airport. Then we get our gears ready and set out for the first day of our trek to Dunai village and pass through the small villages and terraced fields down to the Bheri River. We move along the riverside and and reach the Dunai village. Overnight stay will be at the local tea houses/lodges.

Day 4: TREK DUNAI TO TARAKOT [TREK : 5-6 HRS, 10 KM, 2550 METERS /8336 FT.]
From Dunai we will trek through the terraced fields, gorges, suspension bridges and scattered villages through our trail to the Tarakot village. In the local Nepali language, Kot means Fort and Tarakot village also acted as a fort in the ancient times. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 5: TREK TARAKOT TO LAHINI KHARKA [4-5 HRS. TREK; / 3450 METERS, 11318 FT.]
From Tarakot village we follow the trail through the river and reach the Lahini Kharka. A cave called Lahini Odar is in close proximity. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 6: TREK LAHINI KHARKA TO THULO ODAR [4-5 HRS. TREK; / 3550 METERS, 14435 FT.]
Make a short trek from Lahini Kharka/ Odar to Thulo Odar (3550m) and overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 7: TREK THULO ODAR TO DHO TARAP [TREK; 5-6 HRS / 4050 METERS, 13288 FT.]
Our trail passes through the forested path covered with wild roses and juniper bushes before it reaches the Dho Tarap village.. Dho Tarap in ancient times used to be a hub for trade between, Tibet and Mustang Kingdoms. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 8: DHOTARAP ACCLIMATIZATION DAY [4050 METERS, 13288 FT.]
it is the only time during our trek when we stopover for acclimatization. As we will be crossing two high altitude pass above 5000 meters we need to ensure our body and lungs are ready to do so. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 9: TREK DHO TARAP TO NUMA LA BASE CAMP [TREK; 4 HRS. 8 KM / 4350 METERS, 14271 FT.]
Our trek continues to the Numa La Base Camp through the rugged terrain. On reaching Numa La Base Camp we will Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 10: TREK NUMALA BASE CAMP TO DANIGAR VIA NUMA LA PASS [TREK; 18 KM, 7-8 HRS. / 4550 METERS, 14927 FT.]
It is a long and strenuous day of the trek because on this day we will cross the 1st mountain pass of our trek, the Numa La Pass (5180 meteres, 16995 Ft) and from the top we can witness the majestic panoramic view of himalayan ranges including the Mt. Dhaulagiri and Churen Himal ranges. Then we trek a long way down to the Danigar village. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 11: TREK DANIGAR TO ROMAN KHARKA VIA BAGA LA PASS [TREK; 6 HRS, 19 KM / 4000 METERS, 13123 FT.]
This is another strenuous day of our trek we will be crossing another high altitude pass. After leaving the Danigar village, we will be leaving behind Danigar village and then, we head towards Roman Kharka also popularly known as Yak Kharka. To reach Roman Kharka we need to cross the Baga La Pass (5170 meters, 16961 feet) . We can see the view of Himalayan vistas and also the Beutiful Phoksundo lake from the Baga La Pass. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 12: TREK ROMAN KHARKA TO PHOKSUNDO LAKE [TREK; 6-7 HRS. 18 KM / 3730 METERS, 9383 FT.]
From Roman Kharka we will now head towards one of our major attraction of the trek, the Phoksundo Lake. We will reach Ringmo village. Like Luphra in Mustang, Ringmo village is popular for its endangered Bon religion. A short walk from Ringmo leads us to the beautiful turquoise colored Phoksundo Lake. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 13: PHOKSUNDO LAKE EXPLORATION [TREK; 6-7 HRS. 18 KM / 3730 METERS, 8760 FT.]
It is a rest day at the Phoksundo Lake to explore the lake surroundings and the Ringmo village. Bon religion is an endangered religion that is still being followed in this Ringmo village, so we can spend the day getting awed by the beauty of the Phoksundo Lake as well as getting to know the Bon religion being followed in the village. Our overnight at tented camp.

Day 14: TREK PHOKSUNDO LAKE TO CHHEPKA [TREK; 6-7 HRS. 18 KM / 2670 METERS, 8760 FT.]
From Phoksundo Lake we trek down to Chhepka village. Before reaching Chhepka village we pass through the Chunuwar and Rechi Village. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 15: TREK CHHEPKA TO JUPHAL [TREK; 6-7 HRS. 18 KM / 2499 METERS, 8198 FT.]
This is the final day of our trek we pass through the Shyangta, Kageni and other small villages before we reach Juphal.

Day 16: FLIGHT TO NEPALGUNJ [FLIGHT; 35 MINUTES ]
After completion of our lower Dolpo trek we will then head to Nepalgunj. . You can use the free time on this day on your disposal for personal activities.

Day 17: FLIGHT BACK TO KATHMANDU [FLIGHT; 1 HRS. ]
After spending a day in Nepalgunj, we will take approx. 1 hrs flight to Kathmandu. You can use the free time on this day on your disposal for personal activities.

Day 18: REST DAY IN KATHMANDU
it is a contingency day in Kathmandu as an precaution to the Juphal Nepalgunj sector flight. As the flight to high mountain regions are highly dependent on weather conditions there might cancellation in flights due to bad weather. So contingency day helps us to ensure we dont miss the international flight. This day can be used for personal activities, shopping and also some sightseeing around the monument sites of Kathmandu valley.

Day 19: DEPARTURE
Our airport representative will help you with checkout procedure and then escort you to the airport for final departure from Nepal for your onward journey.

page.name: Lower Dolpa Trek: Shey Phoksundo Lake & the High Passes of Far-Western Nepal — 19 Days
page.subtitle: Juphal to Phoksundo Lake via Numa La (5,180m) and Baga La (5,170m) passes — 19 days through Shey Phoksundo National Park
page.summary:
The Lower Dolpa Trek covers one of Nepal's most geographically and culturally isolated corridors, traveling from the small STOL airstrip at Juphal through the Bheri River valley, over two passes above 5,000 meters, and down to Shey Phoksundo Lake at 3,730 meters — Nepal's largest lake. The 19-day itinerary is structured around the logistical realities of the region: flights from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, then onward to Juphal, where the trek begins in earnest through terraced farmland and river gorges before the terrain shifts into the arid, high-altitude plateau country of Upper Dolpa's doorstep.

The route passes through Tarakot, an ancient fortified village, and Dho Tarap at 4,050 meters — historically a trade junction between Tibet and the Mustang Kingdom — where a full acclimatization day is built in before the two major passes. Numa La (5,180m) delivers panoramic sightlines to Dhaulagiri and the Churen Himal ranges; Baga La (5,170m), crossed the following day, marks the first view of Phoksundo Lake from above. The lake itself, set beneath steep cliffs and surrounded by snow-covered ridges, is reached via Ringmo village, where the Bon religion — predating Tibetan Buddhism — remains in active practice.

The return follows a different line through Chhepka and back to Juphal, with flights retracing the Nepalgunj–Kathmandu axis. A contingency day in Kathmandu is built into the itinerary to account for the weather-dependent nature of mountain flights in this sector. Throughout the trek, accommodation is fully tented camp, consistent with the absence of lodge infrastructure in the more remote sections of the route.

page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Kathmandu: Airport Transfer and Hotel Check-In
On arrival at Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport, the group is met and transferred to the hotel for check-in and overnight.

Day 2 — Kathmandu to Nepalgunj by Air (150m / 492ft)
An early morning flight from Kathmandu takes approximately one hour to reach Nepalgunj, in the Terai lowlands of far-western Nepal. On arrival, the trekking crew meets the group and transfers everyone to Hotel Batika. The remainder of the day is free to walk through Nepalgunj's local markets and streets before overnight at the hotel.

Day 3 — Nepalgunj to Juphal by Air, then Trek to Dunai (2,150m / 7,053ft)
A 35-minute mountain flight on a STOL aircraft lands at Juphal airstrip. From there, the first trekking day begins through small villages and terraced fields, descending to the Bheri River and following the riverbank to Dunai village. The walk takes approximately 3–4 hours. Overnight is at local teahouses or lodges in Dunai.

Day 4 — Dunai to Tarakot Along the Bheri River Gorge (2,550m / 8,336ft)
The trail out of Dunai crosses terraced farmland and passes through scattered villages, traversing gorges and suspension bridges over approximately 10 km and 5–6 hours of walking. The destination, Tarakot, occupies the site of an ancient fortified settlement — the Nepali word 'kot' means fort — and the village retains its historically strategic position above the river corridor. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 5 — Tarakot to Lahini Kharka via the River Trail (3,450m / 11,318ft)
From Tarakot, the route follows the river trail to Lahini Kharka. A cave known locally as Lahini Odar lies close to the campsite. The walk takes 4–5 hours. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 6 — Trek Lahini Kharka to Thulo Odar
A short trek of 4–5 hours ascends from Lahini Kharka to Thulo Odar, situated at 3,550 meters. The route offers gradual elevation gain through alpine terrain. Overnight accommodation is at a tented camp.

Day 7 — Thulo Odar to Dho Tarap Through Juniper and Wild Rose Forest (4,050m / 13,288ft)
The trail to Dho Tarap passes through forested terrain covered with wild roses and juniper before opening onto the village at 4,050 meters. Dho Tarap served historically as a trade junction between Tibet and the Mustang Kingdom, and its architecture and cultural character reflect that cross-border heritage. The walk takes approximately 5–6 hours. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 8 — Acclimatization Day at Dho Tarap (4,050m / 13,288ft)
A full rest day at Dho Tarap is the only scheduled acclimatization stop on the itinerary. The following two days involve crossing passes above 5,000 meters, and the day at altitude here allows the body to adjust before those demanding sections. The village itself can be explored during the day. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 9 — Dho Tarap to Numa La Base Camp (4,350m / 14,271ft)
The route continues across rugged terrain for approximately 8 km over 4 hours to reach Numa La Base Camp at 4,350 meters, in preparation for the following day's pass crossing. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 10 — Numa La Base Camp to Danigar via Numa La Pass (5,180m / 16,995ft) — 18 km
The longest and most demanding day of the trek covers approximately 18 km over 7–8 hours. The route climbs to Numa La Pass at 5,180 meters, where clear conditions provide panoramic views across the Dhaulagiri massif and the Churen Himal ranges to the south and east. The descent from the pass is extended, dropping to Danigar village at 4,550 meters. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 11 — Danigar to Roman Kharka via Baga La Pass (5,170m / 16,961ft) — 19 km
A second consecutive high-pass day covers 19 km over approximately 6 hours. Leaving Danigar, the route climbs to Baga La Pass at 5,170 meters — also referred to as Yak Kharka in local usage — where the first aerial view of Phoksundo Lake becomes visible below to the west. Wide Himalayan panoramas open across the ridge before the descent leads to Roman Kharka at 4,000 meters. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 12 — Roman Kharka to Phoksundo Lake via Ringmo Village (3,730m / 12,237ft) — 18 km
The 18 km descent over 6–7 hours brings the route down to Ringmo village, where the Bon religion — one of Nepal's oldest surviving spiritual traditions, predating the spread of Tibetan Buddhism — remains in active practice among the local community. A short walk from Ringmo reaches the shore of Phoksundo Lake, with its characteristically deep turquoise water. Overnight at tented camp beside the lake.

Day 13 — Rest and Exploration Day at Phoksundo Lake and Ringmo Village (3,730m)
A full day at Phoksundo Lake allows time to walk the lake perimeter, visit the Phoksundo Waterfall — one of the highest in Nepal — and spend time in Ringmo village learning about Bon religious practice, which continues here in monasteries and in daily community life. The lake sits at 3,730 meters, backed by steep cliffs and high snow-covered ridgelines. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 14 — Phoksundo Lake to Chhepka via Chunuwar and Rechi (2,670m / 8,760ft)
The return route descends from Phoksundo Lake through Chunuwar and Rechi villages before reaching Chhepka at 2,670 meters. The walk takes approximately 6–7 hours over 18 km. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 15 — Chhepka to Juphal via Shyangta and Kageni Villages (2,499m / 8,198ft)
The final trekking day follows approximately 18 km over 6–7 hours through Shyangta, Kageni, and further small villages before arriving back at Juphal, the airstrip settlement where the trek began. Overnight at Juphal.

Day 16 — Juphal to Nepalgunj by Air (35-Minute Flight)
A 35-minute mountain flight from Juphal returns the group to Nepalgunj. The remainder of the day is at leisure for personal activities.

Day 17 — Nepalgunj to Kathmandu by Air (1-Hour Flight)
An approximately one-hour flight from Nepalgunj returns the group to Kathmandu. The remainder of the day is free for personal activities or rest.

Day 18 — Kathmandu: Contingency Day for Mountain Flight Disruptions
This day functions as a scheduled buffer against weather-related flight cancellations on the Juphal–Nepalgunj sector, which is susceptible to disruption due to high-altitude weather conditions. If the itinerary has proceeded without delays, the day is available for sightseeing at Kathmandu Valley monument sites, personal shopping, or rest before the international departure the following morning.

Day 19 — Kathmandu: International Departure
An airport representative assists with checkout and escorts the group to Tribhuvan International Airport for onward departure from Nepal.

source.summary:
The Mardi Himal Trek is an absolute choice for those who are seeking for an adventurous trekking experience in the peaceful parts of the Annapurna region of Nepal, spectacularly situated in the east of popular treks of Nepal.  Thin Numbers of trekkers make their way to the Mardi Himal Base Camp out positioned exceptionally at the base of Mardi Himal and the Annapurna region´s most exemplary mount Machapuchhre actually gives meaning "Fish tail", leading mesmerizingly up to with maximum altitude of 4500m. After reaching at high camp (3850m), it takes 3-4 hours to arrive. Mardi Himal base camp.

On top of this, we’ll get to pass by the solitary trails complete with verdant forests, beautiful villages, valleys, terraced farms, dazzling rivers and the extraordinary views of the Annapurna, Machhapuchre (Fishtail) and Himchuli mountains. Another merit about this trekking route is that the trail makes a small circuit up to the base camp of Mardi Himal so that we don’t have to backtrack over the same terrain. Therefore, Mardi Himal Trek a moderate to adventurous trip without the problem of getting AMS (Acute Mountain Sickness.  Because of amalgamation of the adventure and natural delights, it is the brilliant journey.

Accommodation

In our package, accommodation in Kathmandu, 3 star categories of Hotels are made available. Likewise, accommodation in trekking days is in Tea Houses. Our guide will choose a best and regular using normal guest houses, lodges and home stay as per necessity if any. Besides, your guide will help you to choose foods. We ensure you the quality services.

Physical fitness and experiences required

For its completion based on your schedule or fitness level, this trek requires a moderate level of fitness as we’ll have to trek through rocky section near base camp and high camp. Our clients are recommended to see a doctor before they go for a check-up and to talk about dealing with altitude sickness. Trekkers will have to initially decide on their self adjustment of weather changes and also schedule changes in itinerary beyond our control. Experience would be plus point for trekkers. Basic medical helps are our responsibility. Besides, trekkers are advised to carry their medicines if any prescribed earlier by doctors.

Best time to trek

October to May is the most visited season to Mardi Himal base camp. This trek is suitable all year round as the winter brings out the real beauty of the snow-capped peaks and the summer brings out the beauty of the pine, rhododendron and bamboo forest. Hence, October is the best time to start with.

page.name: Mardi Himal Trek: Base Camp Circuit — 10 Days
page.subtitle: A moderate trek in the Annapurna region reaching 4,500 meters, with a circuit route that avoids backtracking and passes through rhododendron forests and traditional Nepalese villages.
page.summary: The Mardi Himal Trek traces a circuit through the Annapurna region east of Nepal's better-known trekking corridors, ending at Mardi Himal Base Camp at 4,500 meters. The route moves through rhododendron and pine forest, past terraced farms and village settlements, and along ridges offering views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain), Annapurna South, and Himchuli. Because the trek follows a loop rather than an out-and-back path, the descent passes through different terrain—including the traditional village of Siding—rather than retracing the ascent. The trek reaches its highest point in 3 to 4 hours from High Camp (3,850 meters), and the moderate fitness level required reflects the altitude gain and rocky sections near base camp rather than technical difficulty. October through May sees the most trekkers on this route; winter snow reveals the peaks clearly while summer brings rhododendron and bamboo in full growth. Accommodation combines 3-star hotels in Kathmandu and Pokhara with tea houses and homestays during the trekking days.
highlights: Trek to Mardi Himal Base Camp at 4,500 meters with views into the Annapurna Sanctuary
Ascent through rhododendron forest to High Camp at 3,700 meters with views of Annapurna South and Himchuli
Circuit descent through Siding, a traditional Nepalese village, and the Brahmin settlement of Kalimati
Sightings of Danphe pheasant and dzokpo (yak-cow crossbreds) on the high ridges
Traversal of the Mardi Himal ridge above tree line on grass and alpine terrain
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Kathmandu
Arrival at Tribhuwan International Airport followed by hotel transfer. An evening briefing outlines the trek itinerary and logistics. Overnight accommodation in Kathmandu.

Day 2 — Kathmandu to Pokhara by Road
A 6- to 7-hour drive westward from Kathmandu to Pokhara passes through towns including Thankot, Naubise, Baireni, Muglin, and Maleku. The journey is typically scheduled early to avoid daytime traffic. Pokhara, situated at the base of the Annapurna range alongside Phewa Lake, serves as the launching point for the trek. Overnight accommodation in Pokhara.

Day 3 — Kande to Pitam Deurali and Forest Camp
A drive from Pokhara reaches Kande, where the trek begins. The initial ascent to Dhampus is steep; the path then eases as it continues to Pothana, passing through mixed forest. Overnight at a tea house in Pothana.

Day 4 — Pothana to Low Camp
A 5-hour trek climbs from Forest Camp to Low Camp at 3,150 meters through rhododendron and moss-covered forest, with occasional glimpses of ferns and lichen on the trees. As elevation increases, the forest composition shifts noticeably. Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) comes into view up the valley. Overnight at Low Camp tea house.

Day 5 — Low Camp to High Camp on the Mardi Himal Ridge
The trail climbs approximately one hour to 3,700 meters, where it breaks above the tree line onto grass slopes and ridges. The route continues along the Mardi Himal ridge, mostly on open grass with scattered rhododendron bushes. Views open westward to Annapurna South and Himchuli. Danphe pheasant are observed on this section. Accommodation is in well-maintained tea houses or lodges at High Camp.

Day 6 — Mardi Himal Base Camp and Return to Low Camp
An early start allows for sunrise views before breakfast. From High Camp, the path follows the ridge crest toward Mardi Himal Base Camp at 4,500 meters, with a few steeper sections through grass. Dzokpo (yak-cow crossbreds) and Danphe pheasant inhabit the high pastures; sheep and goats from lower villages are brought up to graze seasonally. At 4,500 meters, the Annapurna Sanctuary spreads into view—the south face of Annapurna, surrounding peaks, Himchuli, and Machhapuchhre fill the panorama. The return to Low Camp allows for overnight rest and acclimatization.

Day 7 — Low Camp to Siding via Circuit Descent
A 6-hour trek descends from Low Camp along a different route from the ascent, completing the circuit. The path drops to Siding, a traditional Nepalese settlement that remains apart from main trekking circuits. Overnight accommodation is often in a homestay, allowing direct contact with village life and daily routines. Evening meals typically include dal bhat (lentil rice), the staple of Nepalese home cooking.

Day 8 — Siding to Pokhara via Lumre
The trek descends 3 hours from Siding to the roadhead at Lumre, passing through the villages of Kalimati and Ghalel. Kalimati is primarily Brahmin, with mixed populations in Ghalel and Siding. A jeep or similar vehicle completes the 2-hour drive back to Pokhara. Overnight accommodation in Pokhara.

Day 9 — Pokhara to Kathmandu
After breakfast, a tourist bus returns travelers to Kathmandu (approximately 6 hours). A farewell dinner at a local restaurant features Nepalese food and traditional dance. Overnight in Kathmandu.

Day 10 — Departure
Transfer to Tribhuwan International Airport for departure, or onward travel within Nepal if arranged.

source.summary: Swat Valley, often called the 'Switzerland of Pakistan,' is a place of extraordinary natural beauty with its lush green meadows, pine forests, crystal-clear rivers, and snow-capped mountains. This tour takes you through the most scenic parts of this enchanting valley, including the popular hill station of Malam Jabba, the charming town of Kalam, and the stunning Mahodand Lake. You'll also explore the rich cultural heritage of Swat, visiting ancient Buddhist stupas, the Swat Museum, and traditional Swati villages. The tour offers a perfect blend of natural beauty, cultural experiences, and outdoor activities in one of Pakistan's most accessible and picturesque regions.

page.summary: Swat Valley sits in northern Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, a region of steep forested ridges, clear rivers, and meadows that rise toward the Hindu Kush. The valley's primary town, Mingora, anchors the route; from there, roads climb to Malam Jabba, a ski resort, and to Kalam, a smaller mountain settlement used as a base for trekking and lake visits. The valley holds considerable Buddhist archaeological history—ruined stupas and carved sites dating to the 1st century CE remain visible across the landscape. This five-day itinerary combines these elements: museum visits and site walks in Mingora, highland views and short hikes from Malam Jabba, and a full-day excursion to Mahodand Lake. The route follows the Swat River for much of its length and involves mixed terrain—paved valley roads, steep mountain passes, and rough jeep tracks to the lake. Accommodation consists of hotels and guesthouses in the three main towns; guides are English-speaking; meals and entrance fees are included.

Ancient Buddhist stupas and ruins en route to Malam Jabba — carved stone from the 1st century CE
Malam Jabba Ski Resort — panoramic views of the valley and surrounding ridgelines
Drive through Swat River valley to Kalam — a scenic route through forested passes and alongside water
Mahodand Lake full-day excursion — accessible by jeep with optional boating
Bahrain market in the valley — local crafts and traditional goods en route to Islamabad

source.itineraries:
DAY 01 
LUANG PRABANG
Chomphet and Phou Luang Tai (L)
Today we Cycle and trek in Chomphet district across the river from the main Unesco zone of Luang Prabang. We start with a boat downstream to the village Pak Long. From here we cycle to the village of Ban Som (12) and begin an uphill trek to Ban Phou Luang Tai and an extremely remote Hmong Community. It is a 6km trek taking approx. 3 hours.

The community is totally off the grid with no running water, no electricity and just a small primary school.  There are 35 families and  281 people. living a timeless existence perched on the mountainside.

The village is due to be relocated soon as part of the Lao Government's commitment to providing all Lao citizens with access to clean water, electricity, health care and sanitation. From our conversations with the community, the families are all looking forward to a connected and healthier lifestyle. This traditional, symbiotic existence will soon become harder to see in Laos and Phou Luang Tai is an exquisite example of Community and Nature in harmony. Relocation is slated to begin in 2024.

After lunch in the village, trek back down the mountain, approx 90 minutes. We then ride a looping circuit of about 20 km medium biking on dirt roads with some hills and stream crossings. 

You'll be well off the beaten path and into a side of Luang Prabang that few foreigners explore.  This village will soon be gone so this is a limited-time experience.

A professional guide accompanies you every step of the way.

A boat ride downriver precedes a 12km cycle to Ban Som, followed by a 6km, three-hour uphill trek to Ban Phou Luang Tai—a Hmong community of 35 families and 281 people living without electricity, running water, or road access. The settlement sits on a mountainside in what residents describe as a timeless existence; the Lao government has committed to relocating the community by 2024 to provide access to clean water, electricity, health care, and sanitation. page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Cycling and Trek to Ban Phou Luang Tai
Depart from central Luang Prabang by boat, traveling downstream to the village of Pak Long. From there, cycle 12km on dirt roads through Chomphet District farmland to Ban Som, where the uphill trek begins. The ascent to Ban Phou Luang Tai covers 6km over approximately three hours, climbing to a remote Hmong community perched on the mountainside. The settlement comprises 35 families and 281 people living without electricity, running water, or school services beyond a small primary school. The community exists in relative isolation, dependent on subsistence farming and traditional practices. The Lao government has committed to relocation and infrastructure development—electricity, clean water, and sanitation—with moves scheduled to begin in 2024. Following a midday meal in the village, descend the mountain over roughly 90 minutes. The return to the lower elevations follows a looping circuit of approximately 20km on dirt roads, including some hills and stream crossings. Throughout the day, an English-speaking guide navigates the route and facilitates conversations with community members. The cycling portion is moderate terrain with the dirt surfaces and gradients typical of rural Laotian backcountry roads.

source.name: Citadel Rajasthan With Architectural Wonders And The Ganges
highlights:
Destination:- Neemrana, Samode, Jaipur, Kishangarh, Pushkar, Chandelao, Jodhpur, Narlai, Ranakpur, Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Bundi, Bandarej, Agra, Mathura/Vrindavan, Gwalior, Orchha, Khajuraho, Varanasi, Delhi

Major Attractions: Old & New Delhi Sightseeing, Historical Palaces/Forts, The Taj Mahal, Ganges Boat ride, Mughal architecture, Elephant ride at Amber Fort, Camel Safari over Sand Dunes, Visit of 5 UNESCO world Heritage sites, Colourful culture of North India, Rural Villages, Ancient Temples, 1000 Years Old Step Wells, Desert Sunset & Sunrise
source.itineraries:
Day 1 : Delhi - Neemrana: Welcome to Incredible India!

You will be welcomed at Delhi international airport and transferred straight to Neemrana. On arrival; check in at your beautiful heritage hotel. Rest of the day kept at leisure.
Day 2 : Samode

Morning you may take a village walk and visit the nearby step-well. Later proceed straightway to Samode. On arrival, check in your beautiful “Samode Palace”. Evening you may enjoy the walking tour in the village or may enjoy a camel ride at Sand Dunes. Enjoy the dusk at desert on camel’s back.
Day 3 : Excursion to Jaipur

After breakfast proceed for the excursion of Jaipur. Visit the splendid Amber Fort and Maharaja's City Palace (the home of the erstwhile royal family). Later visit the signature building of Jaipur i.e. Hawa Mahal (the Palace of winds) and then enjoy rickshaw ride in the old city. Stay overnight at your palace hotel.
Day 4 : Kishangarh

After a leisurely breakfast proceed towards Kishangarh. Enroute you may enjoy lunch at ‘Pachewargarh Fort’- a 300 years old Fort, situated in a lively little village namely Pachewar. Later you will be transferred straightway to your beautiful heritage hotel named as ‘Phool Mahal’. Kishangarh is mainly known for its world famous Miniature Paintings & Handicrafts. It also has the largest marble and granite cutting industry in India. During the day you may enjoy a visit of many old havelis (mansions) and local colourful makets.
Day 5 : Excursion to Pushkar

Morning proceed to visit the famous Dev Narayana Temple at Dev Doongri. It is believed to be the only place in the world with a temple of nine planets. Later proceed for an excursion to one of the holiest cities of Rajasthan i.e. Pushkar. On arrival, take a walk on the street around the sacred pond and ghats up to Brahma temple. Later visit the Akbar's Palace and Mausoleum. Return to Kishangarh by evening and stay overnight in your hotel.
Day 6 : Chandelao

Morning after breakfast drive to Chandelao. Chandelao village is located just 40 kms ahead from Jodhpur city on the edge of the Thar Desert. On arrival, check in at ‘Chandelao Garh Fort’. Evening you may enjoy a visit to the local village to get a first hand impression of 'Rural India'. Chandelao Village is a typical Rajasthani village where you will find Tibel community. You may get to see the local craftsmen at work viz. the goldsmith, the blacksmith and the weaver during your visit. The village also has three beautifull lakes where you may see a modest variety of birds.
Day 7 : Excursion to Jodhpur

Morning proceed for an excursion to the sun city of India “Jodhpur”. On arrival, visit the magnificent Mehrangarh fort and Jaswant Thada. Later you may enjoy a walking tour to the old markets around Clock Tower. Return back to Chandelao by the evening. After brief leisure you may visit the famous bazaars of Pipar. The Pipar Bazaar is renwoned for ethnic items and local crafts. Here you may also visit the Block Printers. Stay overnight at your heritage hotel.
Day 8 : Narlai

Morning proceed to Narlai passing through scenic landscape of Aravalli hill ranges. On arrival, check in your beautiful palace hotel, situated in the serene forest. After brief leisure enjoy a visit to Khejarla Village where Bishnoi community habitats in multitude. It is really interesting to observe their rustic way of life and rituals. Later you will be visiting a nearby village namely Salawas. It is well known for producing durries, bed covers, carpets, rugs and tents using Camel/Goat hair, wool & cotton. Stay overnight at your hotel.
Day 9 : Excursion to Kumbhalgarh & Ranakpur

Morning move for an excursion to Kumbhalgarh. On arrival visit the beautiful Kumbhalgarh fort.

Later you will be driven to Ranakpur to visit the incomparable Ranakpur Jain temple- the huge 15th century Adinatha Temple. It is among the biggest Jain Temples in India. Return back to Narlai by evening and stay overnight at your palace hotel.
Day 10 : Udaipur - Chittorgarh

Morning after breakfast drive to Udaipur- one of the most romantic cities of India (also known as the Lake City). After checking in, you may visit the Bharatiya Lok Kala Museum (has an interesting collection of dresses, turbans, musical instruments, dolls, paintings, the traditional puppets etc.) and Shilpgram craft village.

In the second half, visit the City Palace & Saheliyon ki Bari. Later drive to Chittorgarh and check in at your heritage hotel.
Day 11 : Chittorgarh

Morning proceed to visit Chittaurgarh Fort - the symbol of Rajput pride and honour. Also visit the Vijay Stambh & Sanwalia Seth temple – a famous temple of ‘lord Krishna’. Interestingly, the local farmers here make the deity partner in their earnings & very religiously donate the share of the deity to the temple on a regular basis. Later you may visit a village school.
Day 12 : Bundi

After breakfast drive towards Bundi - a charming old town. En route visit the Mendalgarh Fort and beautiful temples of Bijalyan & Menal. On arrival, check in at your heritage hotel. Remaining day is at leisure till next morning.
Day 13 : Bundi

Post breakfast proceed to visit Bundi which includes the impressive Taragarh Fort and the characteristic palace complex where the Chitrashala has some of the finest miniature paintings in India. Later visit the nearby temple village of Keshorai Patan for an interesting Deep Daan ceremony in which women chant songs and prayers and float diya candle lamps on the river. Bundi is also famous for its stepwells and water buildings which can be visited in the evening and there are also tribal villages nearby.
Day 14 : Bhandarej

Morning drive to Bhandarej passing through small towns/villages and a series of fields. On arrival, check in at Bhandarej Palace which has an excellent blend of Mughal & Rajputana architecture. The nearby Bhangarh village with its temples and historical sites has a history which dates back to 11th century. After brief leisure enjoy a visit to Abhaneri village to see the most famous step well of Rajasthan.
Day 15 : Agra

Morning after breakfast drive to Agra en route visiting Fatehpur Sikri – once the capital city of Mughal Empire. Finally reach Agra and check in at your hotel. After brief leisure enjoy a guided sightseeing tour of Agra Fort.
Day 16 : Excursion to Mathura & Vrindavan

At dawn proceed to visit the magnificent Taj Mahal. Later proceed for the excursion to Mathura- one of the biggest pilgrimage destinations in India Mathura is believed to be the place where Lord Krishna had grown up. Later you will be visiting Vrindavan. You will visit Govind Dev Temple, Rangaji Temple, Madan Mohan Temple, Glass Temple and Bankey Bihari Temple (one of the oldest temples in India) during the day.
Day 17 : Orchha

Early morning, you may visit the amazing backside view of Taj Mahal across the Yamuna River. Post breakfast you will be driven to Orchha. En route visit the marvelous Gwalior Fort. Later drive towards Orchha - a historical site located on the banks of Betwa River. On arrival, check in your hotel and stay overnight.
Day 18 : Orchha

Morning after breakfast enjoy a sightseeing tour of Orchha including visit of Raj Mahal Palace, Raj Praveen Mahal Palace, Jehangir palace and the Royal Chhattries (cenotaphs). Later visit the Raja Ram temple - only place in India where Lord Rama is worshipped as a king. Stay overnight at your hotel.
Day 19 : Khajuraho

Morning after breakfast drive straightway to Khajuraho. On arrival, check in at your hotel. After brief leisure enjoy the visit of western group of temples. Later visit the eastern group of temples famous for their erotic sculptures. Evening Sound & Light show (English version) is highly recommendable here. Interestingly, Khajuraho is also a nice place for someone who loves Wood-fire Pizzas as it has some nice roof-top Italian restaurants.
Day 20 : Khajuraho - Fly to Varanasi (Kashi)

Morning board a flight to Varanasi. Varanasi is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities of the world and also known as 'Kashi' & 'Banaras'. After brief leisure, visit Sarnath to visit the Buddhist temple and Stupa. Evening enjoy a boat ride over mighty river Ganga to witness the Ganga worship ceremony from a close quarter. Stay overnight at your hotel.
Day 21 : Varanasi (Kashi)

Morning enjoy a boat ride over river Ganges. Later proceed for a sightseeing tour of Varanasi city, which includes visit to Bharat Mata temple, Durga temple, Benaras Hindu University, Vishwanath Temple and a museum i.e. 'Bharat Kala Mandir' which has collection of 12th century’s old manuscripts, miniature painting and sculptures. Evening at appropriate time you will be transferred to Varanasi railway station to board an overnight train to Delhi.
Day 22 : Delhi

On arrival at Delhi railway station you will be assisted and will be transferred to your hotel/guest house to wash-change & brief leisure. Later at appropriate time you will be transferred to Delhi international airport for your onward journey. The tour ends here.

page.name: Rajasthan & the Ganges: Forts, Temples & River — 22 Days
page.subtitle: From Delhi through Rajasthan's palaces and deserts to Varanasi on the Ganges, visiting five UNESCO World Heritage sites across 22 days.
page.summary: This 22-day itinerary traverses northern India from Delhi through Rajasthan's network of fortified cities, temple towns, and desert villages, before descending to the Ganges Valley and Varanasi. The route connects ten major stops—Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Agra, and others—each hosting significant architecture from Mughal, Rajput, and Jain periods. Travellers visit five UNESCO World Heritage sites including the Taj Mahal, Khajuraho temples, and multiple fort complexes. The journey balances large towns with smaller heritage hotels in lesser-known towns like Narlai, Bundi, and Orchha, and includes optional activities in rural villages, camel safaris in desert regions, and boat rides on the Ganges. The final leg moves by train from Varanasi to Delhi.

Taj Mahal at dawn near Agra, a UNESCO World Heritage site
Mehrangarh Fort in Jodhpur overlooking the old city and desert landscape

Kumbhalgarh Fort, a fortified complex in the Aravalli hills near Udaipur
Chittorgarh Fort, a symbol of Rajput military architecture
Fatehpur Sikri, a 16th-century Mughal capital, near Agra
Sarnath Buddhist temple and stupa near Varanasi
Camel safaris across the Thar Desert near Samode and Chandelao
Rural village visits in Bishnoi and Tibel communities
Orchha's palace complexes on the banks of the Betwa River
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Delhi to Neemrana
Arrival at Delhi International Airport and transfer to Neemrana Check-in at a heritage hotel in Neemrana. Remainder of the day is unscheduled.

Day 2 — Neemrana to Samode: Village Walks and Desert Exploration
Optional morning village walk near Neemrana, including a visit to a nearby step-well. Onward travel to Samode, a village settlement on the edge of the Thar Desert. Check-in at a heritage palace hotel. Optional evening activities include a walking tour through Samode village or a camel ride across desert terrain, with views at dusk.

Day 3 — Jaipur Excursion: Amber Fort, City Palace & Hawa Mahal
Morning excursion to Jaipur. Visit Amber Fort, a hilltop complex overlooking the city, with optional elephant rides available. Tour the City Palace, the former residence of the royal household and still partly inhabited. Visit Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds), the five-storey pink sandstone structure well-known to Jaipur's skyline. Afternoon rickshaw ride through the old city market areas. Overnight at a heritage hotel in Jaipur.

Day 4 — Jaipur to Kishangarh: Pachewar Fort and Marble Country
Travel from Jaipur to Kishangarh Lunch stop at Pachewargarh Fort, a 300-year-old structure in Pachewar village. On arrival in Kishangarh, check-in at a heritage hotel. Kishangarh is a centre for miniature painting and Indian marble-and-granite cutting industries. Optional afternoon or evening visits to local havelis (traditional mansions) and market areas. The town's markets sell local textiles, handicrafts, and marble items.

Day 5 — Pushkar Excursion: Temples and the Sacred Pond
Morning visit to Dev Narayana Temple at Dev Doongri, a temple complex dedicated to the nine celestial bodies. Afternoon excursion to Pushkar, a pilgrimage town Walking routes around the sacred pond and ghats lead to Brahma Temple, one of few temples in India dedicated to Brahma. Visit Akbar's Palace and Mausoleum on the town's outskirts. Return to Kishangarh by evening. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 6 — Chandelao: Desert Village and Crafts
Travel to Chandelao, a village 40 kilometres from Jodhpur on the edge of the Thar Desert. Check-in at a heritage fort hotel. Chandelao is a rural Rajasthani settlement with a Tibel community presence. Optional evening visits to local craft workshops—blacksmiths, goldsmiths, and weavers—demonstrate traditional techniques. Three nearby lakes support modest bird populations. The village environment offers views of typical rural Rajasthani settlement patterns and agricultural land.

Day 7 — Jodhpur Excursion: Mehrangarh Fort and Clock Tower Markets
Morning excursion to Jodhpur, approximately 40 kilometres away. Visit Mehrangarh Fort, a large fortified complex dominating the city's skyline, and Jaswant Thada, a 19th-century marble cenotaph nearby. Walking tour of the old city markets around the Clock Tower. Optional visit to Pipar Bazaar, known for local textiles and block-printing workshops. Return to Chandelao by evening. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 8 — Narlai: Aravalli Foothills and Community Villages
Travel to Narlai through the Aravalli hill ranges, passing agricultural and forested terrain. Check-in at a heritage palace hotel in a forest setting. Afternoon visit to Khejarla Village, where the Bishnoi community resides. The Bishnoi practice specific agricultural and spiritual traditions centred on environmental protection and animal welfare; visitors may observe village routines and daily life. Evening visit to Salawas village, known for production of traditional carpets, rugs, and textiles woven from camel hair, goat hair, wool, and cotton. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 9 — Kumbhalgarh & Ranakpur: Forts and Jain Temples
Morning excursion to Kumbhalgarh Fort, a fortified hilltop complex in the Aravalli range. Afternoon travel to Ranakpur to visit the Adinatha Temple, a large 15th-century Jain structure The temple is one of the largest Jain temples in India. Return to Narlai by evening. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 10 — Udaipur: City Palace, Museums & Lake City
Travel to Udaipur Check-in at a hotel. Visit Bharatiya Lok Kala Museum, housing traditional dress, turbans, musical instruments, puppets, and paintings from Rajasthani culture. Visit Shilpgram, a craft village with demonstrations and sales of local textiles and handmade items. Afternoon tour of the City Palace, a complex of courtyards and rooms overlooking Lake Pichola, and Saheliyon ki Bari (Garden of the Maidens), a formal garden with fountains and pavilions. Late afternoon travel to Chittorgarh Check-in at a heritage hotel.

Day 11 — Chittorgarh: Fort and Temple Complex
Morning visit to Chittorgarh Fort, a large hilltop structure with multiple palaces, temples, and water tanks spanning several centuries of Rajput architecture. Visit Vijay Stambh (Tower of Victory), a tall commemorative tower within the fort complex, and Sanwalia Seth Temple, dedicated to Lord Krishna. Optional visit to a local village school. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 12 — Bundi: Journey to the Old Town
Travel to Bundi En route, visit Mendalgarh Fort and temples at Bijalyan and Menal. Check-in at a heritage hotel in Bundi's old quarter. Remainder of day at leisure.

Day 13 — Bundi: Palaces, Miniature Paintings & Stepwells
Morning visit to Taragarh Fort, a fortified hill structure, and the adjacent palace complex featuring the Chitrashala, a room with miniature paintings from the Bundi school. Afternoon visit to Keshorai Patan village temple. Evening optional viewing of the stepwells and water structures for which Bundi is known. These include Raniji ki Baoli, a multi-storey stepwell. Optional visit to nearby tribal villages. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 14 — Bhandarej: Mughal and Rajput Architecture
Travel to Bhandarej, passing small towns, villages, and agricultural fields. Check-in at Bhandarej Palace, a structure blending Mughal and Rajput architectural styles. Optional afternoon visit to Bhangarh village, featuring temples and historical structures dating to the 11th century. Evening visit to Abhaneri village to see Chand Baoli, a large stepwell with multiple levels of arched recesses, among the largest stepwells in Rajasthan. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 15 — Agra: Fatehpur Sikri & Agra Fort
Travel to Agra En route, visit Fatehpur Sikri, a walled city built in the 16th century as a Mughal capital and later abandoned. The site contains palaces, courtyards, and mosques. Arrival in Agra and check-in at a hotel. Afternoon guided tour of Agra Fort, a large riverside complex with multiple palaces and walls. Overnight at hotel.

Day 16 — Taj Mahal, Mathura & Vrindavan: Religious Sites
Early morning visit to the Taj Mahal, a marble mausoleum built in the 17th century. The structure is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Travel to Mathura, a major pilgrimage destination believed to be associated with Krishna's childhood Visit temples including Govind Dev Temple, Rangaji Temple, Madan Mohan Temple, and Bankey Bihari Temple, one of the oldest temples in the town. Afternoon or evening visit to Vrindavan, an adjacent pilgrimage town. Optional visit to Glass Temple. Overnight in Agra.

Day 17 — Gwalior Fort & Orchha: River Palace Towns
Optional early morning visit to the Taj Mahal from the Yamuna River's far bank. Midday travel to Orchha En route, visit Gwalior Fort, a large hilltop fortress with palaces and temples. Arrival in Orchha, a historical settlement on the Betwa River. Check-in at a hotel. Overnight at hotel.

Day 18 — Orchha: Palaces and Royal Temples
Morning sightseeing tour of Orchha, including Raj Mahal Palace, Raj Praveen Mahal Palace, and Jehangir Palace, all part of a palace complex built over centuries. Visit the Royal Chhatris, cenotaphs of former rulers. Afternoon visit to Raja Ram Temple, a shrine where Lord Rama is worshipped as a ruling monarch rather than a deity alone. Overnight at hotel.

Day 19 — Khajuraho: Temple Complexes and Sculptures
Travel to Khajuraho Check-in at a hotel. Afternoon visit to the Western Group of temples, a cluster of structures built between the 10th and 11th centuries. Visit the Eastern Group of temples, also dating to the medieval period and notable for their sculptural detail. Evening Sound and Light show (English narration) at one of the temple complexes. Overnight at hotel.

Day 20 — Varanasi: Flight, Sarnath & Ganges Boat Ride
Morning flight to Varanasi, a city on the Ganges River and one of the oldest continuously inhabited settlements in the world. Check-in at a hotel. Afternoon visit to Sarnath, approximately 10 kilometres away, home to a Buddhist temple and stupa marking the location where Buddha taught. Evening boat ride on the Ganges to observe the Ganga Aarti, an evening ritual performed at the water's edge. Overnight at hotel.

Day 21 — Varanasi: City Temples, University & River
Early morning boat ride on the Ganges to observe sunrise and ghats (riverside steps). Morning sightseeing tour of Varanasi including Bharat Mata Temple, Durga Temple, Vishwanath Temple, and Banaras Hindu University. Visit Bharat Kala Mandir, a museum housing manuscripts, miniature paintings, and sculptures from the 12th century onward. Evening transfer to Varanasi railway station to board an overnight train to Delhi.

Day 22 — Delhi: Arrival and Departure
Morning arrival at Delhi railway station. Transfer to a hotel or guest house for rest and wash. Afternoon or evening transfer to Delhi International Airport for onward travel. Tour concludes.

source.name: THE BEST OF WEST & CENTRAL BHUTAN
source.subtitle: Route: Paro → Thimphu → Punakha → Trongsa → Bumthang → Tang Valley → Gangtey → Wangdi → Paro
source.itineraries:
DAY 1   Arrival in Paro.
Your tour guide will meet you and take you on a short one-hour drive along the Paro and Thimphu river valleys to Thimphu, Bhutan's capital, at 2320 metres. You can stop on the way to take in the magnificent Tamchhog Lhakhang, the hereditary place of worship for Bhutan's iron bridge builder.
Overnight in Thimphu
DAY 2   Sightseeing in Thimphu.
We can visit the weekly market, the National Memorial Chorten, the Buddha Dordenma, Changangkha Temple, Takin Reserve, the School of Traditional Arts and Crafts, the Folk Heritage Museum, and the National Library. Browse the striking collection of intricate textiles at the National Textile Museum and visit the craft bazaar. Discuss your preference for the day with the guide.
Overnight in Thimphu
DAY 3   Drive to Punakha via Dochu La Pass, where we will stop for a hot drink and enjoy views of the Eastern Himalayan range.
In the afternoon visit Chimi Lhakhang (Temple of Fertility), built in the 15th century by the 'Divine Mad Man' (Lama Drukpa Kunley) and Punakha Dzong.
Overnight in Punakha
DAY 4   Drive from Punakha to Bumthang via Trongsa, the gateway to central Bhutan.
You can stop to visit the impressive Trongsa Dzong which commands the eye from miles away. Visit the museum in the watchtower dedicated to the Royal Wangchuk dynasty, which tells the stories of the Dzong and features personal belongings of the Kings and Queens of Bhutan. Continue your journey through some of Bhutan's most beautiful landscapes to Bumthang.
Overnight in Trongsa
DAY 5   A day of sightseeing in the Bumthang valleys.
Your guide will take you on a fascinating tour of a variety of sacred sites including Jamba Lhakhang, Kurjey Lhakhang and Tamshing Lhakhang. Visit Jakar Dzong (Bhutan's largest) and you may be interested to see Bumthang's famous Swiss cheese factory or the Red Panda Brewery.
Overnight in Bumthang
DAY 6   Today we take an excursion to the remote Tang valley.
Stop to visit Membar Tsho (the burning lake), which is one of Bhutan's most important pilgrimage sites. Then on to Drangchel, Pema Lingpa's birthplace. You will also see some picturesque villages and temples and can walk up to visit Ugyencholing Palace, which is now a museum and gives an interesting insight into life in an aristocratic family in the last century.
Overnight in Tang Valley
DAY 7   Start your journey back west to Gangtey in the remote Phobjikha valley.
Visit Gangtey Gompa (one of Bhutan's oldest monasteries and extensively renovated) and explore the valley where the villagers continue to live a traditional Bhutanese rural lifestyle. This is the site where black-necked cranes visit in their hundreds in November each year after spending the summer in Tibet.
Overnight in Gangtey
DAY 8   Today can be a day of leisure in this beautiful rural valley.
If it is winter you can view the black-necked cranes. If you like hiking your guide will suggest a day or half day hike in the valley.
Overnight in Gangtey
DAY 9   Return to Paro via Wangdi.
Wangdi Dzong, built by the Shabdrung in 1638 on an auspicious site where four ravens were seen flying in four different directions, was badly damaged in a fire in June 2012 but has been painstakingly renovated over 12 years and is now open to visit. When you reach Paro you can visit the local handicraft shops for souvenirs of your trip.
Overnight in Paro
DAY 10   Sightseeing in Paro.
Visit Dumtse Lhakhang, The National Museum, Paro Rinpung Dzong and Kyichu Lhakhang (temple).
Overnight in Paro
DAY 11   Take a day hike to the 'Tiger's Nest', the sacred Taktshang Monastery.
You can stop at the Taktshang cafeteria viewpoint on the way up for a wonderful view of the monastery.
Overnight in Paro
DAY 12 (Departure)
Depart from Paro International Airport with a full heart.

page.name: West and Central Bhutan: Dzongs, Valleys and Mountain Passes — 12 Days
page.subtitle: From Paro through Punakha, Bumthang and Gangtey, following dzongs and sacred sites
page.summary: This 12-day circuit moves systematically through Bhutan's administrative and spiritual core, beginning in the Paro valley and moving east through the country's major dzongs — fortress-monasteries that anchor each region's governance and religious practice. The route crosses Dochu La Pass into Punakha, continues east to Bumthang's valleys and the Tang region, then descends west through Phobjikha's black-necked crane habitat before returning to Paro. Days are structured around named sites — Trongsa Dzong's royal museum, Jakar Dzong (Bhutan's largest), Taktshang Monastery's clifftop setting — rather than generic scenic loops. The itinerary accommodates seasonal variation: winter visitors may see black-necked cranes in Phobjikha; summer travellers encounter clearer mountain views and accessible higher trails.
highlights: Trongsa Dzong's museum, featuring personal belongings of Bhutan's royal dynasty
Taktshang Monastery, the sacred monastery above Paro valley
Jakar Dzong, Bhutan's largest fortress, dominating Bumthang's agricultural plains
Membar Tsho (Burning Lake), a pilgrimage site associated with Pema Lingpa's treasure revelation
Phobjikha valley's black-necked crane habitat and Gangtey Gompa, one of Bhutan's oldest monasteries
Dochu La Pass crossing with views of the Eastern Himalayan range
Ugyencholing Palace museum in Tang valley, preserving aristocratic life from the last century
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Paro to Thimphu via Tamchhog Lhakhang
A one-hour drive from Paro valley northward along the Paro and Thimphu rivers reaches Bhutan's capital, positioned at 2,320 metres. The route passes Tamchhog Lhakhang, a temple and hereditary residence associated with Bhutan's legendary iron bridge builder. Thimphu itself spreads across a high valley floor without walls or administrative boundaries—an administrative capital designed around Buddhist planning principles rather than colonial precedent.

Day 2 — Thimphu: Temples, Museums and Markets
Thimphu's sightseeing options centre on the capital's religious and cultural institutions. The National Memorial Chorten anchors the city's centre; the colossal Buddha Dordenma statue overlooks the valley from a ridge; Changangkha Temple sits on a hilltop with city views. The National Textile Museum houses an extensive collection of traditional Bhutanese weaving, while the Folk Heritage Museum and School of Traditional Arts document rural craftsmanship. The weekly market and craft bazaar provide context for understanding local textiles, produce and handicrafts. Your guide will recommend a selection based on your interests.

Day 3 — Dochu La Pass to Punakha Dzong
The drive south crosses Dochu La Pass, with stops for views of the Eastern Himalayan range and a hot drink. Descending into Punakha's warmer valley, visit Chimi Lhakhang, the 15th-century temple built by Lama Drukpa Kunley, and Punakha Dzong, where two rivers converge.

Day 4 — Trongsa and the Gateway to Central Bhutan
The eastward drive from Punakha moves into Bhutan's central region via Trongsa, a fortress-town positioned on a dramatic ridge overlooking river gorges. Trongsa Dzong commands landscape views for kilometres in all directions. The site includes a watchtower museum dedicated to the royal Wangchuk dynasty, displaying personal possessions of Bhutan's kings and queens alongside the dzong's architectural and political history. From Trongsa, the road continues through forested, steep terrain toward Bumthang's valleys.

Day 5 — Bumthang's Sacred Sites and Jakar Dzong
The day's sightseeing visits three major temples—Jamba Lhakhang, Kurjey Lhakhang and Tamshing Lhakhang—each connected to Bhutanese Buddhist history and pilgrimage practice. Jakar Dzong, Bhutan's largest fortress-monastery, dominates the valley centre. The region supports a Swiss cheese factory and Red Panda Brewery, both established by expatriates and now integrated into local agricultural routines. Your guide can suggest time allocation based on your interests.

Day 6 — Tang Valley: Remote Pilgrimage Sites and Palaces
A full-day excursion into the remote Tang valley visits Membar Tsho, a lake with rock overhangs that pilgrims associate with the treasure revealer Pema Lingpa. The site is one of Bhutan's most important pilgrimage destinations. Continuing deeper into the valley reaches Drangchel, Pema Lingpa's birthplace, and Ugyencholing Palace, now a museum documenting aristocratic family life in rural Bhutan during the last century. The valley itself contains scattered villages and smaller temples. A walk to Ugyencholing requires modest hillside climbing.

Day 7 — Gangtey Gompa and Phobjikha Valley
The westward journey returns to Phobjikha valley, where Gangtey Gompa sits on a hillside overlooking the wetland. The monastery, one of Bhutan's oldest, underwent extensive renovation in recent decades. The surrounding valley remains largely rural, with farming communities maintaining traditional agricultural practices and settlement patterns. Phobjikha is notable as the winter habitat for black-necked cranes, which arrive in November from their summer grounds in Tibet and depart in March.

Day 8 — Phobjikha Valley: Rest Day or Optional Hiking
This day accommodates seasonal variation and individual pacing. Winter visitors can observe black-necked cranes in their hundreds across the valley floor. Summer travellers, or those preferring active time, can hike a half-day or full-day route suggested by your guide through the valley's rural landscape and forests.

Day 9 — Return to Paro via Wangdi Dzong
The westward drive to Paro passes through Wangdi, site of Wangdi Dzong, built by the Shabdrung (Bhutan's unification figure) in 1638. The fortress sustained severe fire damage in 2012 and underwent twelve years of restoration before reopening. The drive continues west and downward into Paro valley. Upon arrival, handicraft shops in Paro offer souvenirs and locally produced textiles, art and crafts.

Day 10 — Paro Valley Temples and Museums
Paro's sightseeing includes Dumtse Lhakhang, the National Museum of Bhutan, Paro Rinpung Dzong and Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest temples.

Day 11 — Taktshang Monastery Hike
The hike to Taktshang Monastery (also called Tiger's Nest) ascends a path from Paro valley to a monastery on a cliff face. The route passes a cafeteria viewpoint offering close views of the monastery's whitewashed walls and gold-topped chapels before the final approach.

Day 12 — Departure from Paro International Airport
Depart from Paro International Airport, carrying memories of your journey.

source.name: North India Revealed
source.summary: Embark on a 22-day odyssey through India’s intoxicating north. Discover sights, smells, and flavours that will blaze their way into your memory and stay there forever. See towering sandstone fortresses, pilgrims praying on riverbanks, Maharajah mementos in a ghostly palace, and silhouettes on a desert landscape. India can be a daunting place at times, even for experienced travellers, but with the guidance of your local leader, you’ll be navigating the crowds, dodging the cows and eating the best chaat from a cart in no time! From the beating heart of Delhi to the holy city of Varanasi – this is north India.
source.itineraries:
Day 1  Delhi
Namaste and welcome to Delhi! Your adventure begins with a welcome meeting at 6 pm. If you arrive in Delhi with time to spare before the meeting, consider finding your feet with an Urban Adventure. The Hidden Gems of Delhi tour offers something a little different from the standard itinerary, taking you to sights most tourists never see.
Day 2  Delhi – Overnight Train
This morning set off by metro to Old Delhi to explore on a walking tour. Experience the chaos of an Indian traffic jam as you inch your way through the streets around Chandni Chowk marketplace in a traditional cycle rickshaw. Visit the Jama Masjid, Delhi's oldest mosque, then stop by the Sheeshganj Gurudwara (Sikh Temple) to learn about the religion. Tonight, transfer to the railway station and board an overnight train to Bikaner. Local vendors will board the train at various stops to sell snacks, but it’s advised that you bring some of your own food for the journey too.
Day 3  Bikaner
Bikaner a city in Rajasthan still displays its ancient opulence through palaces and forts, built of red sandstone that have withstood the passage of time. Upon arrival in Bikaner this morning, freshen up at your hotel and then head out on a walk with your leader through the old city.

In the afternoon relax or opt to visit Junagarh Fort: Built in 1588 AD by Raja Rai Singh. Constructed in red sandstone and marble, it's courtyard, balconies and windows are a treat to the eye
Day 4  Bikaner to Jaisalmer
After breakfast travel to Jaisalmer by train. On arrival, choose whether to relax or join the group on an optional trip to the Jaisalmer Folklore Museum. This small museum displays a private family collection of printing blocks, musical instruments, religious artifacts, and decorations which offer insights into the cultural heritage of Jaisalmer.
Day 5  Jaisalmer
Enjoy a free day to explore Jaisalmer. The city’s eponymous fort holds twisting alleys with markets where you can wander for hours. You can also find a series of Jain temples dating from the 15th and 16th centuries within the walls of the fort, and it’s easy to spend a few hours admiring their elaborate carvings. The opulent havelis (traditional Indian mansions) found throughout the city make another fine place to spend some time admiring the desert architecture.
Day 6  Thar Desert
Today drive by jeep to the Thar Desert. Meet your local guides, who will cook a traditional Rajasthani dinner with chapati, dal, rice and veggies while you sit back, relax and watch the sunset. Spend the night stargazing and sharing stories in this incredible setting.
Day 7  Jodhpur
Rise early to enjoy the sunrise over the sand dunes. After a simple breakfast, take a private vehicle to the railway station and then a 6-hour train ride across the desert to the blue city of Jodhpur. Jodhpur is home to some of the best lassis in India, so make sure you try one while you’re here.
Day 8  Jodhpur
Today you have the option to visit the colossal Mehrangarh Fort, one of the largest in India. The fort is still run by the Jodhpur royal family. If you’d prefer to see a more down to earth kind of Rajasthani life, it is also possible to spend today touring nearby Bishnoi villages. Spending time in these villages offers a glimpse into rural Rajasthani life and the chance to learn about the rich cultural traditions of the people who live there.
Day 9  Udaipur
This morning take an auto-rickshaw to the bus station and board a local bus for an 8-hour journey to Udaipur. This romantic city is set amid the Aravalli Hills and curls around Lake Pichola, a man-made lake created in the 14th century. On arrival, take a guided walk to get your bearings. Explore twisting alleyways filled with shops and bazaars selling things like silver jewellery, shoes, bags, leather goods, and miniature paintings.
Day 10 Udaipur
Enjoy a free day to explore the sights of Udaipur. Perhaps take a short boat ride on the famous Lake Pichola (seasonal) and see the palaces of Jag Mandir and Jag Niwas rise out of the water and their own reflections. Otherwise, you could tour the lakeside City Palace complex, the largest palace in Rajasthan, where you can check out vivid murals and royal antiques. Alternatively, learn the secrets behind making the perfect Indian thali during a half-day cooking class.

Maybe you’d like to visit Sajjan Garh (Monsoon Palace), a 19th-century palace perched on a hill overlooking Lake Pichola. Named after Maharana Sajjan Singh of the Mewar Dynasty, Sajjan Garh offers ridiculously great views of the city below. Or perhaps you’re more inclined to visit the nearby village of Shilpgram, an ethnographic museum and arts hubs where traditional crafts are sold, and artists perform.
Day 11  Pushkar
Transfer to the station and travel by train for around 5.5 hours to the city of Ajmer. Hop in a private vehicle for a 45-minute drive to your hotel in Pushkar. One of India's holiest towns and a market centre for the surrounding villages, Pushkar is a great place to immerse yourself in Hindu traditions. On arrival, head out to explore the town on a walking tour, wandering through the main bazaar along the way. Finish with a walk around Pushkar Lake and past the bustling ghats and temples, observing the devout as they worship at the holy waters.
Day 12  Pushkar
Today in Pushkar is free for you to do as you please. Early morning risers can choose to hike up the hill to the Savitri Temple for sunrise views over the town. If the chai man is there, enjoy a steaming cup of tea at the top for breakfast. Later in the day, maybe pay a visit to the colourful Brahma Temple, which is dedicated to the Hindu god. If you’ve planned your tour to coincide with the Pushkar Camel Fair (which changes each year), today will mainly be set aside to experience one of India’s most famous festivals.
Day 13 Jaipur
Return to Ajmer and travel by local bus to Jaipur (approximately 4 hours). On arrival take an auto-rickshaw to your hotel, then head out to explore Rajasthan’s capital on a guided walking tour. This tour includes a visit to the market and opt to visit the beehive-like Palace of the Winds (Hawa Mahal), built in 1799 so that women of the royal family could observe street festivities without being seen by the public. Your evening is free, so perhaps ask your leader to point out the best place to grab dal baati (dal served with wheat rolls).
Day 14  Jaipur
Enjoy a free day in Jaipur, with plenty of optional activities to choose from to fill your day. For many travellers, an optional hot air balloon experience is one of the highlights of Jaipur. If you’d prefer to stay grounded (but still like expansive views) the Amber Fort is both an excellent example of Rajput architecture and a great place from which to see the surrounding area. Or maybe get among the crowds in the city’s bazaars to shop for artisan goods and semi-precious stones. For a true local experience, tonight you could immerse yourself in Bollywood with a movie at a classic cinema.
Day 15  Abhaneri
Head to Abhaneri by private vehicle. This rural town provides a lovely detour from the bigger cities in Rajasthan. Visit the Chand Baori, a 20-metre-deep stepwell where water was collected and locals used to gather to escape the heat. Built in the late ninth century, the baori is a mind-bending feat of construction. Next visit another jewel of Abhaneri, the Harshat Mata Temple. This temple, which is now mostly ruined, was first constructed between the seventh and eighth centuries and dedicated to the goddess of happiness and joy.
Day 16  Fatehpur Sikri – Agra
Head east by private transport for the 2–3-hour journey to Agra, via a stop Fatehpur Sikri where you can opt to go inside. Rich in Mughal heritage, Agra is a city of gardens, temples, and open rooftops. On arrival visit the Taj Mahal, a white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a memorial to his wife Mumtaz. One of the New Seven Wonders of the World, the Taj Mahal attracts over three million visitors each year, so be prepared for crowds. If you’re after a cool drink or a light meal, maybe head to Sheroes Hangout. This cafe is staffed by survivors of acid attacks and is located 10 minutes’ walk from the Taj.
Day 17  Agra – Overnight Train
Enjoy a free day before boarding the train this evening. Early risers might want to head back to the Taj Mahal for a very memorable sunrise. While you’re here, be sure to visit the spectacular Red Fort on the banks of the Yamuna River. Built in 1565 by Emperor Akbar, the fort was originally designed to be a military structure. If you have extra time, you may like to continue onto Akbar's Mausoleum to pay your respects to the great emperor. In the evening, board a 12-hour overnight train to Varanasi (Third Class AC).
Day 18  Varanasi
On arrival in Varanasi this morning transfer by auto-rickshaw to your hotel. Head out on a guided walk around the Old City, following your leader through the narrow alleyways. The rest of your day is free to do as you please. This evening, there are two options you should consider, both centred around the holy Ganges. The first is a sunset cruise along the river which allows you to observe life from a unique perspective in the fading light of day. If you’d prefer to stay on land, you could watch local priests perform a Ganga aarti (fire ceremony) at the Dashashwamedh Ghat.
Day 19  Varanasi
Enjoy a free day to explore this holy city. We highly recommend starting very early and take an optional sunrise boat trip along the Ganges, passing pilgrims bathing and praying along the colourful ghats. Alternatively, head out to the ghats on foot to watch the dhobi-wallahs (clothes washers) drying clothes along the riverbank. You could even continue your stroll to the sinking Vishnu temple near the Manikarnika Ghat. Perhaps ask your leader about how to visit Sarnath, about ten kilometres outside of the city, where Gautama Buddha is said to have given his first speech after finding enlightenment.
Day 20  Varanasi – Overnight Train
In the morning, you have some free time to explore more of Varanasi. Perhaps visit the Vishwanath Temple, or simply grab some chaat and watch the world go by. If you’re craving a little peace and quiet before you board another overnight train, consider heading to the Kriti Gallery to check out some contemporary work by local artists. In the afternoon, board the overnight train for a 15-hour journey to Delhi.
Day 21  Delhi


Arrive in Delhi in the late morning and hop in a taxi to the hotel. The rest of the day is free for you to relax or explore the city at your own pace. Tonight, maybe get together with your group and head out for some dinner – your local leader will have plenty of recommendations.
Day 22  Delhi
With no activities planned for today, your North India adventure comes to an end. You are free to depart the accommodation at any time.
