page.name: North India: Delhi to Varanasi — 22 Days
page.subtitle: From the capital's layered neighborhoods to the Ganges ghats and Rajasthani desert forts — a 22-day overland journey by train, bus, and local transport
page.summary: This 22-day itinerary moves through northern India's major cities and regions, from Delhi's Old City markets to the Rajasthan circuit of Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, and Udaipur, then eastward to the temple towns of Pushkar and Jaipur, the ruins of Fatehpur Sikri and Agra's Taj Mahal, and finally to Varanasi on the Ganges. The route combines guided urban walks through busy bazaars and historic quarters, overnight trains between destinations, visits to palaces and forts built in red sandstone and marble, a night camping in the Thar Desert, and time spent watching pilgrims at temples and ghats. A local guide leads the entire journey; accommodation ranges from hotels and guesthouses to overnight sleeper trains and one night of desert camping. The pace allows for both structured exploration and free time within each city to wander independently or participate in optional activities such as cooking classes, boat rides, and visits to lesser-known villages and archaeological sites.
highlights: Walking tour through Old Delhi's Chandni Chowk marketplace and cycle rickshaw ride through congested streets
Junagarh Fort in Bikaner — 1588 red sandstone and marble structure with ornate courtyards and balconies
Desert camp and sunrise in the Thar Desert near Jaisalmer with traditional Rajasthani dinner
Mehrangarh Fort in Jodhpur — one of India's largest forts, still managed by the Jodhpur royal family
Lake Pichola in Udaipur — 14th-century man-made lake with lakeside palaces and boat access
Chand Baori stepwell in Abhaneri — 20-metre-deep 9th-century structure with geometric precision
Taj Mahal in Agra — white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan, one of the New Seven Wonders
Sunrise and sunset boat rides on the Ganges in Varanasi with views of bathing pilgrims and temple ghats
Ganga aarti fire ceremony at Dashashwamedh Ghat in Varanasi — daily ritual performed by local priests
Jain temples within Jaisalmer Fort — 15th and 16th-century structures with elaborate stone carvings
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Delhi
Arrival in Delhi marks the beginning of the journey. A welcome meeting is scheduled for 6 pm at the hotel. Travellers arriving with time before the meeting may visit the city independently or join an optional urban walking tour of lesser-known areas outside the standard tourist circuit.

Day 2 — Old Delhi by Metro and Cycle Rickshaw
The morning begins with a metro journey to Old Delhi for a walking tour. A cycle rickshaw ride through the streets surrounding Chandni Chowk marketplace provides direct experience of Indian traffic and street life. Stops include the Jama Masjid, Delhi's oldest mosque, and the Sheeshganj Gurudwara, a Sikh temple where visitors learn about the religion and its practices. In the evening, transfer to the railway station for an overnight sleeper train to Bikaner. Local vendors board the train at various stops to sell snacks; travellers are advised to bring additional food for the journey.

Day 3 — Bikaner — Red Sandstone Palaces and Forts
Upon arrival in Bikaner in the morning, time is allowed to rest at the hotel before a walking tour through the old city with the local guide. Bikaner displays its historical wealth through palaces and forts constructed from red sandstone. In the afternoon, visitors may relax or visit Junagarh Fort, built in 1588 by Raja Rai Singh using red sandstone and marble. The fort's courtyards, balconies, and carved windows exemplify Rajput architectural design.

Day 4 — Train Journey to Jaisalmer
After breakfast, travel by train to Jaisalmer. Upon arrival, visitors may rest or opt to visit the Jaisalmer Folklore Museum, a small collection of private family artifacts including printing blocks, musical instruments, religious objects, and traditional decorations that document the cultural heritage of the region.

Day 5 — Jaisalmer Fort and Havelis — Free Exploration
The day is unstructured, allowing independent exploration of Jaisalmer. The fort itself contains twisting alleys and markets that can occupy several hours of wandering. Within the fort walls stand Jain temples dating from the 15th and 16th centuries, featuring elaborate stone carvings. Throughout the city, opulent havelis — traditional Indian mansions — showcase desert architecture and interior decoration.

Day 6 — Thar Desert Camp with Sunset and Stars
A jeep drive transports visitors to the Thar Desert, where local guides prepare a traditional Rajasthani dinner of chapati, dal, rice, and vegetables. The evening is spent watching the sunset and spending the night under open sky, with time for conversation and stargazing.

Day 7 — Desert Sunrise and Train to Jodhpur
An early departure allows observation of sunrise over the sand dunes. After a light breakfast, a private vehicle carries the group to the railway station for a six-hour train crossing the desert to Jodhpur, known as the blue city. Jodhpur is noted for traditional lassi — a yogurt-based beverage — available throughout the city.

Day 8 — Jodhpur — Mehrangarh Fort or Bishnoi Villages
The day offers two primary options. Mehrangarh Fort, one of India's largest, remains under management by the Jodhpur royal family and contains extensive architecture and palace rooms. Alternatively, visits to nearby Bishnoi villages provide exposure to rural Rajasthani life and allow observation of traditional cultural practices and agricultural systems in the region.

Day 9 — Auto-Rickshaw and Bus to Udaipur
An auto-rickshaw carries travelers to the bus station for an eight-hour local bus journey to Udaipur. The city sits within the Aravalli Hills and curves around Lake Pichola, a man-made lake created in the 14th century. On arrival, a guided walk provides orientation through the twisting alleyways and bazaars selling silver jewellery, shoes, bags, leather goods, and miniature paintings.

Day 10 — Udaipur — Palaces, Lake, and Optional Activities
This day is free for independent exploration of Udaipur's many sites. A short seasonal boat ride on Lake Pichola offers views of Jag Mandir and Jag Niwas palaces rising from the water. The lakeside City Palace complex, the largest palace in Rajasthan, contains vivid murals and royal antiques. A half-day cooking class teaches the preparation of Indian thali. Sajjan Garh, a 19th-century palace on a hilltop overlooking Lake Pichola and built by Maharana Sajjan Singh, provides expansive views of the city. The nearby village of Shilpgram functions as an ethnographic museum and arts hub where traditional crafts are sold and artists perform.

Day 11 — Train to Ajmer, then Pushkar — Holy Town on the Lake
A train journey of approximately 5.5 hours departs for Ajmer, followed by a 45-minute private vehicle drive to Pushkar. One of India's holiest towns and a market center for surrounding villages, Pushkar is a site of significant Hindu pilgrimage. On arrival, a walking tour leads through the main bazaar and concludes at Pushkar Lake, where devout worshippers bathe and pray at the bustling ghats lined with temples.

Day 12 — Pushkar — Optional Temple Hike and Free Exploration
The day is unscheduled. Early risers may hike to Savitri Temple on a hilltop for sunrise views over the town; local vendors often sell tea at the summit. Later, the Brahma Temple, a colorful structure dedicated to the Hindu god Brahma, is open for visits. If the tour dates align with the Pushkar Camel Fair — an annual festival that changes dates yearly — significant time is devoted to experiencing one of India's largest fairs.

Day 13 — Local Bus to Jaipur and City Walking Tour
A return to Ajmer is followed by a local bus ride of approximately four hours to Jaipur, Rajasthan's capital. An auto-rickshaw takes the group to their hotel; a guided walking tour follows, including visits to the city market and an optional stop at the Palace of the Winds (Hawa Mahal), built in 1799 to allow royal women to observe street events unseen. The evening is free to wander independently; the local guide can recommend dining options.

Day 14 — Jaipur — Amber Fort, Bazaars, and Optional Hot Air Balloon
Jaipur offers numerous optional activities on this free day. Many travellers choose an optional hot air balloon flight for views over the surrounding landscape. Amber Fort, an outstanding example of Rajput architecture, sits on elevated terrain and provides expansive views of the surrounding area. The city's bazaars offer artisan goods and semi-precious stones for purchase. A visit to a classic cinema showing Bollywood films provides a local cultural experience.

Day 15 — Abhaneri — Chand Baori Stepwell and Harshat Mata Temple
A private vehicle transports the group to Abhaneri, a rural town offering a departure from Rajasthan's larger cities. The Chand Baori stepwell — a 20-metre-deep structure built in the late ninth century — demonstrates remarkable engineering precision and served as a water collection and cooling refuge for residents. The Harshat Mata Temple, mostly ruined but originally constructed between the seventh and eighth centuries, was dedicated to the goddess of happiness and joy.

Day 16 — Fatehpur Sikri Detour and Arrival in Agra
A 2-3 hour private vehicle journey heads eastward to Agra, with an optional stop at Fatehpur Sikri, a 16th-century Mughal city. Agra, rich in Mughal heritage, contains gardens, temples, and open rooftops throughout its streets. On arrival, a visit to the Taj Mahal — a white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a memorial to his wife Mumtaz — is made. One of the New Seven Wonders of the World, the Taj Mahal draws over three million visitors annually; crowding is substantial. Sheroes Hangout, a cafe 10 minutes' walk from the Taj staffed by acid attack survivors, offers refreshments.

Day 17 — Agra — Red Fort, Akbar's Mausoleum, and Overnight Train
The day is free for exploration. Early risers may return to the Taj Mahal at sunrise. The Red Fort, built in 1565 by Emperor Akbar on the banks of the Yamuna River and originally designed as a military structure, contains extensive architecture and courtyards. Akbar's Mausoleum is located further along the same region. In the evening, a 12-hour overnight sleeper train (third-class air-conditioned) departs for Varanasi.

Day 18 — Varanasi Arrival and Ganges Options
Arrival in Varanasi occurs in the morning. An auto-rickshaw transfers visitors to their hotel, followed by a guided walk with the local guide through the narrow alleyways of the Old City. The remainder of the day is free. Two evening options center on the Ganges River: a sunset boat cruise providing views of life along the water in fading daylight, or attendance at a Ganga aarti — a fire ceremony performed by local priests — at Dashashwamedh Ghat.

Day 19 — Varanasi — Ganges Ghats and Optional Sarnath
This day is unscheduled. An optional early-morning boat trip along the Ganges passes pilgrims bathing and praying along the colorful ghats. Walking to the ghats allows observation of dhobi-wallahs — clothes washers — drying textiles along the riverbank. The partially submerged Vishnu Temple near Manikarnika Ghat can be visited on foot. Sarnath, located approximately 10 kilometers outside the city, is the site where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon after achieving enlightenment; the local guide can provide directions.

Day 20 — Varanasi Morning Exploration and Evening Train
Free time in the morning allows further exploration of Varanasi, including optional visits to the Vishwanath Temple or simply time spent eating chaat — a savory Indian snack — while observing daily life. The Kriti Gallery, displaying contemporary work by local artists, offers a quieter environment. In the afternoon, a 15-hour overnight train departs for Delhi.

Day 21 — Delhi — Arrival and Free Day
Arrival in Delhi occurs in late morning. A taxi carries travelers to the hotel. The remainder of the day is free to rest or wander at individual pace. The local guide can recommend dining options; group dinners are optional.

Day 22 — Delhi Departure
Your North India adventure concludes today. With no scheduled activities, you are free to depart your accommodation at any time that suits your onward travel plans.

source.name: Southern Explorer Cycling Tour
source.subtitle: 440km & 3000m Elevation | Indigenous Villages | Night Markets | Hot Springs
source.summary: On this 8-day tour, guests will experience southern Taiwan's best cycling and scenery. The route is both challenging and rewarding, with a few hot spring hotels for pampering. Explore coastlines, climb mountains, discover indigenous tribes, and savor fresh local cuisine, all while enjoying the journey from the saddle.
highlights:
Fully Supported Bike Tour in Southern Taiwan
Cycling along western and eastern coastlines of Taiwan
Stay overnight in two hot spring hotels, including the famous An Tong Creekside Hot Spring Hotel in Yuli
Visit a Paiwan Indigenous village for exclusive tour and lunch
Cycling in the iconic East Rift Valley surrounded by rice paddies
source.itineraries:
Day One: Kaohsiung | Fangliao (Non-Riding)
Meet your guide in Kaohsiung before transferring by private van to Fangliao. After check-in, guests can explore, relax in the infinity pool, or join a shakedown ride. Staff will assist with bike setup. In the evening, we'll have a Welcome Dinner and debrief.

Day Two: Fangliao to Kenting (57km / 62m / 4 hrs)
After breakfast, we'll ride south from our coastal hotel to the vibrant beach town of Kenting. Starting on flat roads, we'll follow the coastline to Taiwan's southern tip and arrive at Kenting National Park. Our ride ends beachside, followed by dinner and a visit to the lively night market.

Day Three: Kenting to Daren (75km / 1,101m / 6 hrs)
Today is challenging, but the stunning views are worth it. Starting in Kenting, guests will cycle coast to coast, navigating one of Taiwan's most scenic routes. Route 199 offers curvy climbs, followed by a gentle descent to the coast. End the day in a quaint village with a group dinner.

Day Four: Daren - Zhiben (70km / 478m / 4.5 hrs)
After a longer day, Day Four has a short morning ride along Taiwan's stunning east coast. After a Paiwan community tour and lunch, ride to Zhiben, known for its hot springs and National Forest. Guests can relax before a group dinner.

Day Five: Zhiben - Chenggong (86km / 369m / 5 hrs)
Today is all about coastal riding! We'll leave Zhiben, pass through Taitung, and reconnect with the coastal highway, with palm trees, white sand beaches, and Pacific views. After a visit to Sanxiantai Arch Bridge, we'll ride to an oceanfront accommodation, then head to Chenggong for dinner.

Day Six: Chenggong - Yuli (50km / 576m / 4.5 hrs)
Today features one of the bigger climbs, ending in the beautiful East Rift Valley, a cyclists' paradise. We'll ride inland from the coast, over mountains, and into a green valley. After lunch, a short ride takes us to a historic hot spring hotel.

Day Seven: Yuli - Hualien (102km / 394m / 6 hrs)
The final riding day is our longest, with little elevation gain and a steady decline into Hualien City. We'll ride through the scenic East Rift Valley, Taiwan's Rice Basket before lunch in an ecological park. Afterward, we'll ride into Hualien to our hotel and explore Dongdamen Night Market.

Day Eight: Hualien - Taroko - Taipei (Transfer Day)
The final day won't include riding but will be just as spectacular. After breakfast, we'll head up the east coast by private van, exploring Taroko Gorge, Changchun Shrine, and Bulouwun Terrace. We'll visit cliff-side look outs, then end the tour with a group meal at Taiwan's first craft brewery.

page.name: Taiwan's Southern Coastline & East Rift Valley — 8 Days by Bike
page.subtitle: Kaohsiung to Hualien: western and eastern coastlines, mountain passes, and a hot spring stop in the East Rift Valley.
page.summary: This eight-day supported cycling tour traces southern Taiwan's geography from west coast to east across two distinct coastlines and inland mountain terrain. The route begins in Kaohsiung, moves south through Kenting National Park to Taiwan's southern tip, then cuts eastward across Route 199—one of the island's most technical cycling corridors—before descending to the Pacific coast. From there, the tour follows the eastern seaboard northward through Taitung and into the East Rift Valley, finishing in Hualien. Two overnight stays at hot spring hotels in Zhiben and Yuli break the riding days. The itinerary includes a visit to a Paiwan Indigenous village and a guided tour of Taroko Gorge on the final day.
highlights: Ride from Kenting south to Taiwan's southernmost point along the western coastline
Cycle Route 199 across the island's southern ridge.
Visit a Paiwan Indigenous community for a guided tour and shared meal
Soak in overnight accommodations at An Tong Creekside Hot Spring Hotel in Yuli
Ride through the East Rift Valley's rice paddies on the approach to Hualien
View Sanxiantai Arch Bridge from the saddle along Taiwan's eastern Pacific coast
Visit Taroko Gorge's limestone formations and cliff-side lookouts on the final day
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Kaohsiung and Transfer to Fangliao
Meet your guide in Kaohsiung and transfer by private van south to Fangliao, arriving at a coastal hotel. After settling in, you have the option to rest, swim in the infinity pool, or join a short shakedown ride to familiarize yourself with your bike. Hotel staff will assist with any bike setup or adjustments needed. In the evening, gather for a welcome dinner and route overview.

Day 2 — Fangliao to Kenting: Coastline Approach
Depart on mostly flat terrain from Fangliao, following Taiwan's western coastline southward. The road runs close to the water as you approach Kenting, a beach town that marks the edge of Kenting National Park. Ride 57 kilometers in approximately four hours, finishing near the beach. The evening includes dinner and time to visit Kenting's night market.

Day 3 — Kenting to Daren: Crossing the Southern Ridge on Route 199
Today's 75-kilometer route takes you across the island's southern ridge on Route 199, one of Taiwan's most demanding cycling corridors. Begin in Kenting and climb through curving mountain roads, ascending more than 1,100 meters over the course of roughly six hours. After cresting the ridge, descend to the east coast and the village of Daren. The payoff is a complete coast-to-coast traverse of Taiwan's southern width. A group dinner concludes the day.

Day 4 — Daren to Zhiben: Paiwan Village Visit and Hot Spring Arrival
A shorter riding morning of 70 kilometers along Taiwan's east coast follows the previous day's exertion. Visit a Paiwan Indigenous village for a guided tour and shared lunch, learning about traditional practices and local history. Continue to Zhiben, a small town known for its hot springs and proximity to a national forest. The afternoon is free for soaking and rest. Group dinner at your accommodation.

Day 5 — Zhiben to Chenggong: Pacific Coastal Riding
Leave Zhiben heading north, pass through Taitung, and reconnect with the coastal highway. Eighty-six kilometers of riding with relatively modest elevation gain (369 meters) keeps the pace steady as you roll past palm trees, white sand beaches, and Pacific views. Pass Sanxiantai Arch Bridge, a distinctive rock formation visible from the saddle. Arrive at oceanfront accommodation in Chenggong before heading into town for dinner.

Day 6 — Chenggong to Yuli: Climbing into the East Rift Valley
Today's 50-kilometer route climbs 576 meters inland from the coast, transitioning from sea level to the East Rift Valley. Ride over mountain passes and into a green valley marked by rice paddies and quiet roads—terrain that cycling communities often describe as a draw in itself. After lunch, a short final ride brings you to Yuli and An Tong Creekside Hot Spring Hotel, where the evening is yours to relax.

Day 7 — Yuli to Hualien: Final Ride Through the Rice Basket
The longest riding day at 102 kilometers features mostly gentle decline as you move north through the East Rift Valley—locally known as Taiwan's Rice Basket for its patchwork of paddies and farmland. Approximately six hours of riding with only 394 meters of elevation gain keeps the pace manageable. Stop for lunch at an ecological park, then continue into Hualien City and your hotel. Evening visit to Dongdamen Night Market.

Day 8 — Taroko Gorge and Hualien Departure
No riding on this final day. Travel by private van up the east coast from Hualien to Taroko Gorge, exploring the limestone formations, Changchun Shrine, and Bulouwun Terrace. Stop at cliff-side lookouts for views into the canyon system. Return to a group meal at Taiwan's first craft brewery before transferring to the airport or your next destination.

source.summary:
The Lhasa Namtso Lake Tour is an exploration of the historical city of Lhasa and Namtso Lake. Namtso Lake in Tibet is the second-largest lake in Tibet. It is situated 250 Km northern from Lhasa. Namtso lake extent 70 km from east to west and 30 km from south to west. This lake is covering as area of 1920 sq km and is situated at an altitude of 4748 m. Small Himalayan peaks are surrounding and well hanging of Tibetan prayer flags makes more beautiful. This lake is also regarded as a holy Lake in Tibet. Namtso Lake from Lhasa can be a day tour or a night stay at a simple guest house near the lake.

The historical city of Lhasa and sightseeing around is exploring important Tibetan monuments. Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple, Barkhor Street, Drepung Monastery, and Sera Monastery are the listed of most visiting place in Lhasa. Lhasa is connecting with international airport. Flight is only possible from any part of China and from Nepal. It is also connected with the train route from the main cities of China. Touch Kailash Travels and Tours offer a private Lhasa Namtso Lake Tour either direct from China or from Nepal.
highlights:
Historical city Lhasa and sightseeing in the main monuments of Lhasa
Exploration of the 2nd largest and holy Namtso Lake
source.itineraries:
Day 01: Arrive in Lhasa (3650 m/11972ft). Overnight at Hotel
Arrive in Lhasa (Gonggar) airport or train station and be greeted by our airport representative who will escort you to the hotel with 1.5 hrs drive. The rest of day is leisured, acclimatized yourself to high latitude. 

Day 02: Sightseeing in Lhasa. Overnight at Hotel
We begin our sightseeing tour that includes Potala Palace, the greatest monumental structure in Tibet, and it was once the center for both spiritual and temporal power of Tibet. You will be attracted deeply by rooms, halls, chapels, and furnishings of Potala Palace. And the stories that took place there will convulse you absolutely. In the afternoon, we will visit Jokhang Temple which is the holiest Tibet's temples. A palpable sense of reverence accompanies a visit here. The constant bustle, dazzling paraphernalia of worship, flickering butter lamps and wreaths of heady incense make the Jokhang Temple one of Tibet's most memorable experiences. Finally we will visit fascinating Barkhor Street which is Lhasa's liveliest place and it is also the main route for prayer wheels rotating. 

Day 03: Sightseeing in Lhasa. Overnight at Hotel
This morning we make sightseeing tour of the Drepung Monastery which was once Tibet's richest Monastery, with four colleges and 10,000 monks in its heyday in the 17th century. A group of white buildings stands on the hillside and out against the majestic Mt. Gambo Utse, here you can get a wonderful view of the Lhasa City and surrounding scenery. The next sightseeing spot is Sera Monastery. It is famous for its warrior monks, Dob-Doa. After that, we will visit Norbulingka which was once the summer palace of the Dalai Lamas. It contains several palaces, chapels, and buildings. Finally we drive back to the hotel. 

Day 04: Drive Lhasa to Namtso Lake & back to Lhasa. Overnight at Hotel
Drive to visit the second largest salt water lake in China.Namtso Lake is the biggest lake located at the highest altitude in the world. The Lake maintains its levels from rainfall and melted snow flowing from high mountains. Namtso is also popular for being a sacred Buddhist pilgrimage site where Zhaxi Temple is situated. The Lake's beauty should not be missed by any traveler during the visit in Tibet. 

Day 05: Departure from Lhasa
After breakfast you will be transferred to airport to connect flight to Kathmandu or other destinations OR drop to train station.

page.name: Lhasa and Namtso Lake — 5 Days
page.subtitle: Potala Palace, monasteries, and Tibet's second-largest lake at 4,748 meters
page.summary: This five-day itinerary moves between Lhasa's monastic architecture and Namtso Lake, Tibet's second-largest body of water, situated 250 kilometers north of the capital at an altitude of 4,748 meters. The route begins with acclimatization in Lhasa before progressing through the city's major religious sites—Potala Palace, the former seat of temporal and spiritual authority; Jokhang Temple, regarded as Tibet's holiest sanctuary; and the monasteries of Drepung and Sera, which historically housed thousands of monks. A full day is devoted to the drive north to Namtso Lake, where the water body extends 70 kilometers east to west and 30 kilometers south to north, covering an area of 1,920 square kilometers. The lake is encircled by Himalayan peaks and marked as a sacred Buddhist pilgrimage site, with Zhaxi Temple situated on its shores. The itinerary accommodates both day-excursion and overnight options at guesthouses near the lake, returning to Lhasa by evening or the following morning.
highlights: Potala Palace in Lhasa — the former winter residence of the Dalai Lamas, a multi-story monumental structure of halls, chapels, and residential quarters
Jokhang Temple — Tibet's holiest shrine, characterized by ritual activity, butter lamps, and continuous pilgrimage
Drepung Monastery — historically one of Tibet's largest monastic centers, with views across Lhasa valley from its hillside position
Sera Monastery — known for its scholarly tradition and monastic debate practices
Namtso Lake at 4,748 meters — the second-largest saltwater lake in China, ringed by Himalayan peaks and prayer flags
Barkhor Street — the circumambulation circuit in central Lhasa, lined with shops and prayer wheels
Norbulingka — the summer palace complex of the Dalai Lamas, comprising multiple chapels and residential buildings
page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Lhasa
Arrival at Lhasa Gonggar Airport or the main train station, followed by a 90-minute transfer to accommodation in the city. Lhasa sits at 3,650 meters above sea level. The first day is reserved for acclimatization to the altitude; no structured activities are scheduled.

Day 2 — Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple, and Barkhor Street
The morning begins with a visit to Potala Palace, a multi-story complex that served as the winter residence and seat of religious authority for the Dalai Lamas. The structure contains numerous halls, chapels, and chambers arranged across its hillside location. In the afternoon, the itinerary moves to Jokhang Temple, the foremost pilgrimage destination in Tibet. The temple interior is animated by continuous religious activity—devotees circumambulating, butter lamps burning, and incense rising through the galleries. A final stop is Barkhor Street, the principal circumambulation route in central Lhasa, lined with shops, prayer wheels, and pilgrims on circuit.

Day 3 — Drepung, Sera, and Norbulingka
The morning is spent at Drepung Monastery, situated on a hillside overlooking Lhasa. In its seventeenth-century peak, the site housed four distinct colleges and approximately 10,000 monks; its white buildings are clustered against the backdrop of Mount Gambo Utse. The location provides extended views across the Lhasa valley. In the afternoon, the route proceeds to Sera Monastery, recognized for its scholarly monastic tradition and the practice of structured debate among monks. A final stop is Norbulingka, the summer palace complex of the Dalai Lamas, which contains multiple residential and ceremonial buildings arranged as a formal compound.

Day 4 — Namtso Lake Excursion
A full day devoted to the drive north to Namtso Lake, positioned 250 kilometers from Lhasa. The lake, Tibet's second largest, covers 1,920 square kilometers and sits at an altitude of 4,748 meters. The water body is fed by rainfall and snowmelt from surrounding Himalayan peaks, which ring the shoreline. Zhaxi Temple stands on the lake's edge, marking the site as a major Buddhist pilgrimage destination. The route returns to Lhasa by evening, or accommodation at a nearby guesthouse may be arranged for an overnight stay.

Day 5 — Departure from Lhasa
Transfer to Lhasa airport or train station for onward travel to Kathmandu or other destinations.

source.name: Uncover Korea: K Pop & Hanok Villages
source.summary: Join the crew as we hit all the best spots in South Korea. From the markets in Seoul, the hanok village in Jeonju, through the beautiful coast along Busan and the incredible island of Jeju. With bright city lights and relaxing island sights, this tour will make you fall in love with every single thing South Korea has to offer.
highlights:
Explore the best of Seoul at HiKR Ground and Gwangjang Market
Stay overnight in a Hanok Village
Dive into a mountainside full of color with a visit to Gamcheon
Get way off the beaten track and explore Jeju island
source.itineraries:
Day 1   Seoul
Arrive at any time and welcome to South Korea's largest metropolis. There are no activities planned until the evening welcome meeting, so spend the day exploring on your own time. In the evening, meet your group and your CEO at the welcome meeting. After, head out for an orientation walk and welcome dinner to get to know your group and the city of Seoul. After filling up on some delicious Korean food, opt to join your CEO & new friends out on the town for your First Night Out. Maybe grab a beer or choose to test your singing voice at karaoke.

Your First Night Out Moment: Connect With New Friends
Connect with new friends on your first night out in a new destination. Only available on 18-to-Thirtysomethings tours.

Your Welcome Moment: Meet Your CEO and Group
Your opportunity to meet your CEO and fellow travellers, and learn more about your tour. Opt to join the group for a local meal afterwards. Don't forget to see the notice in the lobby (or ask reception) for the official time and place to meet up with the group.

Accommodation
Below is an example of the hotel we may use in this city. For the actual hotel your specific departure will be using, please check your voucher.

Dream Guest House (or similar)  Guesthouse
Meals included: Dinner
Day 2   Seoul
Start your day channeling your inner K Pop star at HiKR Ground. Then head to what may be the cutest street in all of Seoul, Ikseon-Dong Alley. After some shopping, instagrammable moments, and free time for lunch, explore the Gwangjang market and try some iconic Korean snacks. Then enjoy a free evening in the city.

HiKR Ground                 Seoul
Explore the 5 story, immersive experience dedicated to all things Korea. Think K-Pop, K-Drama and the most popular parts of Korean culture. Witness incredible art, listen to your favorite K-Pop band, and learn about Korean pop-culture.

Ikseon-dong Alley          Seoul
Stroll through the narrow alleys of Ikseon-dong where traditional hanok houses, modern cafes and hip restaurants coexist. Relax in quaint cafes or shop in local craft stores while admiring the beautiful hanok architecture. Hop in and out of local boutiques and galleries, stopping at the perfect photo stops at every turn.

Free Time                       Seoul
Enjoy free time in Seoul. Check out N Seoul Tower, Gangnam neighborhood or Han River Park.

Gwangjang Market Visit      Seoul    1h
Gwangjang Market is one of the oldest and largest traditional markets in South Korea, with more than 5,000 shops. Famous for its fabric, local treasures, and noted to be one of the best places to go for authentic Korean street food in Seoul, you don't want to miss Gwangjang Market.

Optional Activities - Day 2

Gangnam District Visit       Seoul
Gangnam has plenty to do and see in this historically rich, fast-developing neighbourhood. Gangnam Station is the busiest subway station in Seoul and has a huge underground shopping centre, so feel free to shop until you drop. Choose to visit Bongeunsa, a Buddhist Temple in the centre of Gangnam, or enjoy the nightlife and restaurants in this area.

N Seoul Tower Visit            Seoul
Take the cable car to visit the most iconic landmark in Seoul! Located at the top of Mt Namsan, and standing at 480m above sea level, what used to be a broadcasting station before it was open to the public, is now a beautiful observatory. If you'd like to go up the tower to the observatory an additional fee is required.

Accommodation
Dream Guest House (or similar)

Seoul is yours to explore today. With endless options, there's no bad way to enjoy this city. Opt to visit the DMZ, take a K Pop dance class, go on a Seoul City Tour or try your hand at some Korean delicacies at a cooking class.

Free Time             Seoul           Full Day
The day is yours to enjoy Seoul as you wish.

Optional Activities - Day 3

Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) VisitDemilitarized Zone (DMZ)
Visit the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) the de facto border between North and South Korea, which cuts the peninsula in half. Created in 1953, it is the most heavily militarized border in the world.

K-Pop Dance Class          Seoul
Channel your inner pop star at a K-pop dance classes. Learn the latest K-pop choreography with professional instructors and feel the energy of K-pop & K-pop culture. Classes are available for various skill levels, so even beginners can participate easily. These classes often end with a recording session, allowing participants to take home a video of their performance as a special souvenir.

page.name: South Korea: Seoul, Hanok Villages & Island — 10 Days
page.subtitle: Seoul to Jeju via Jeonju and Busan, with overnight stays in traditional hanok and visits to Gamcheon, Haedong Yonggung Temple, and Seongsan Sunrise Peak.
page.summary: This 10-day route moves through South Korea's most recognizable cultural landmarks and lesser-trafficked districts in sequence. Begin in Seoul with visits to HiKR Ground and Gwangjang Market, then take the train to Jeonju for an overnight stay in a traditional hanok house in the village's preserved quarter. The itinerary then shifts to the coast: Busan's clifftop Buddhist temple, its markets and cable car, and the pastel-painted houses of Gamcheon stacked on a mountainside. The final three days settle on Jeju Island, where the route includes a guided walk through Seongeup Folk Village, a hike to Seongsan Sunrise Peak, and a performance by haenyeo—traditional female divers who harvest seafood by breath-hold. Free time is built into most days, and optional activities (DMZ visit, K-pop dance class, cooking class) are available in Seoul and scattered throughout.

page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Seoul
Arrive at any time in South Korea's capital and largest metropolis. With no planned activities until evening, you have the day free to visit Seoul independently at your own pace, whether that means wandering neighbourhoods, visiting museums, or simply adjusting to the city.

In the evening, meet your CEO and fellow travellers at the welcome meeting—your opportunity to learn more about the tour ahead and connect with your group. After the meeting, join an orientation walk through Seoul's streets to familiarize yourself with the city's layout and energy.

Dinner follows at a local Korean restaurant, where you'll share your first meal with the group and begin getting to know one another. The evening is yours to shape: those interested can opt to join your CEO and new friends for a First Night Out, exploring Seoul's bar scene or testing your singing voice at karaoke. Participation is entirely optional—if you prefer an early night, that's equally welcome.

Accommodation will be at Dream Guest House or similar.

*Your Welcome Moment: Meet Your CEO and Group—your chance to connect with fellow travellers and learn what lies ahead. Your First Night Out Moment (available on 18-to-Thirtysomethings tours): Connect with new friends as you visit your new destination together.*

Day 2 — Seoul: K-pop, Markets & Street Culture
Begin your morning at HiKR Ground, a five-story immersive space dedicated to Korean pop culture. The exhibition moves through K-pop performances, K-drama media, and contemporary art installations that capture what defines modern Korean culture. From there, head to Ikseon-Dong Alley, a narrow district where traditional hanok houses now sit alongside modern cafes, boutiques, and independent galleries. The architecture creates a distinctive atmosphere—each corner offers something to photograph and wander. Spend time drifting between local craft stores and quaint cafes, getting a sense of how Seoul blends heritage with contemporary life.

Lunch is yours to structure. Continue exploring Ikseon-Dong's cafes and shops, or move ahead to Gwangjang Market at your own pace. Once you arrive at Gwangjang Market, you're in one of Seoul's oldest and largest traditional markets, operating with over 5,000 vendors. The market sprawls across multiple sections: textiles and fabrics fill certain alleys, while other areas concentrate on handicrafts and local treasures. But Gwangjang is most renowned for its street food stalls—this is considered one of Seoul's best places for authentic Korean snacks and casual meals. Plan an hour to navigate the market, try local dishes, and absorb the energy of one of the city's most vital commercial and culinary spaces.

Your evening is unscheduled, leaving room to rest or pursue optional activities. If you want to visit N Seoul Tower, take the cable car up Mt. Namsan to the 480-meter observation deck—an additional fee applies for entry to the observatory. Alternatively, venture into Gangnam District, a historically rich neighborhood now defined by rapid development and constant activity. Gangnam Station itself is the city's busiest subway hub and contains an enormous underground shopping center. The district also hosts Bongeunsa, a Buddhist temple set in the neighborhood's center, and numerous restaurants and nightlife venues if you prefer to spend your evening in this area. Otherwise, simply rest at your accommodation and recharge for the days ahead.

Day 3 — Seoul: A Day of Your Own Design
Seoul is yours to wander at your own pace. With the city's efficient subway system and distinct neighborhoods, there's no bad way to spend your time here.

If you'd like structure, several optional activities are available. Visit the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), the de facto border between North and South Korea and the world's most heavily militarized frontier since its creation in 1953. Or channel your inner pop star at a K-pop dance class, where professional instructors teach the latest choreography at various skill levels. Most classes culminate in a recording session—a special souvenir to take home.

Alternatively, join a guided Seoul City Tour by bus, visiting Gyengbokgung Palace, the National Folklore Museum, Jogyesa Temple, Bukchon Hanok Village, and Insadong Alley. You might also try a Korean cooking class to learn the fundamentals of local delicacies, or simply wander neighborhoods that call to you.

Return to Dream Guest House (or similar) in the evening, having spent the day exactly as you wished.

Day 4 — Train to Jeonju & Hanok Village Overnight
Take the morning train to Jeonju, a city in the southwestern region known for its preserved traditional quarter and often called one of South Korea's prettiest cities. After checking into your hanok accommodation, your CEO leads a walking tour of Jeonju Hanok Village, pointing out key cultural landmarks including the Gyeonggijeon Shrine, Jeondong Catholic Church, Korean Liquor Museum, and Jeonju Handicraft Exhibition Hall. The stroll reveals the beautiful hanok streets and their distinctive traditional architecture, offering an immersive introduction to the area.

The afternoon and evening are yours to wander at your own pace. Wander through Jeonju Nambu Traditional Market to experience local commerce and daily life, or head to the Hanok Village Craft Museum to engage with Korean traditional craftsmanship firsthand. Here you can try your hand at hanji (traditional Korean paper-making), work at the pottery wheel to shape your own ceramic vessel, practice the meditative art of traditional calligraphy with brush and ink, or craft and paint your own decorative Korean fan—choosing from designs like flowers, birds, and landscapes.

If you prefer, visit a local shop to try on a hanbok, the lively traditional Korean dress, and have photographs taken in the picturesque hanok setting. The colorful, layered garments offer an authentic way to experience Korean cultural dress in its most fitting environment.

This evening, settle into the comforts of your traditional hanok house. Built with natural materials and historic architecture, the accommodation offers genuine insight into Korean history and culture—a stay that feels like stepping back in time. The experience of sleeping in a hanok is itself part of your journey through Korea's past, allowing you to absorb the aesthetic and spatial principles that have defined Korean domestic life for centuries.

Day 5 — Busan: Gamcheon Culture Village & Coastal Exploration
Travel by local bus from Jeonju to Busan, a 3-hour, 260-kilometer journey down to Korea's southern coast. Upon arrival, drop your luggage at your accommodation in Nampodong, the lively downtown district, then make your way to Gamcheon Culture Village. This artistic neighborhood clings to a mountainside, its narrow lanes lined with pastel-colored houses, hand-painted murals, small cafes, and independent galleries. The village draws photographers and art lovers alike, offering endless opportunities to wander and see. Spend the late afternoon and early evening exploring the village's atmospheric streets before returning to downtown Busan for the night.

If you prefer a more active evening, two optional activities await. Haeundae Beach is one of Korea's most celebrated stretches of sand—ideal for an evening walk along the shore or a swim, depending on season. Adjacent Dongbaek Island features the APEC House, a distinctive structure built to host the 2005 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Alternatively, experience a traditional Korean jjimjilbang (spa bath house), where you can soak in hot-spring tubs and rejuvenate after your travel day.

Day 6 — Busan: Temples, Cable Car & Markets
Start your day at Haedong Yonggungsa Temple, a striking Buddhist complex built in 1376 and perched on cliffs overlooking the East China Sea. The temple's seaside setting is singular in Korea—legend holds that prayers offered here will grant at least one wish. From the temple, make your way to the Songdo Maritime Cable Car for a one-mile gondola ride up to Songdo Sky Park. The observatory deck provides sweeping views across Busan's coastline and harbor.

In the afternoon, head to Jagalchi Fish Market at Nampo Port, where fishmongers sell fresh seafood from countless stalls. This is where locals come to haggle for the best catch; watching the negotiation unfold offers genuine insight into daily Busan life. Nearby, visit Gukje Traditional Market, set close to BIFF Square (named after the Busan International Film Festival). The market's roots trace back to the Korean War, when it served as a refuge for displaced people seeking livelihood. Today it's a lively bazaar offering food, home goods, clothing, and souvenirs alongside the history.

The remainder of your day is unscheduled, leaving space to rest or wander at your own pace before tomorrow's transfer to the beach.

If you want more activity, two options stand out: Skyline Luge lets you control a kart down a mountaintop track with ocean views—you can ride multiple courses and even try the adjacent zipline or scenic chairlift. Alternatively, Taejongdae Zip Line offers a more intense rush: soar 653 meters above Gamji Beach on one of several thrilling lines suspended over the water.

Day 7 — Flight to Jeju & Dongmun Market
After a free morning in Busan, fly south to Jeju, the subtropical island off Korea's southern tip. Settle into your accommodation in downtown Jeju City, where you'll stay for the next three nights. This evening, join your CEO at Dongmun Market, one of Jeju's most lively traditional markets. The market pulses with energy after dark—neon signs illuminate food stalls, vendors call out their wares, and the air fills with the aroma of grilling black pork, a local specialty. Sample hallabong, Jeju's famous tangerines, and wash them down with fresh orange juice. Keep an eye out for the Red Lobster Fire Dance Show, a street performance that appears among the stalls. The market offers a genuine slice of local culture and flavour; wandering its lanes unguided lets you see what catches your interest. The rest of the evening is yours to wander further or rest after your journey.

Day 8 — Jeju: Folk Village, Sunrise Peak & Haenyeo Divers
Today unfolds as a deep immersion into Jeju's cultural landscape, beginning with the tangible past and ending with living tradition.

Start with a guided tour of Seongeup Folk Village, a living museum that preserves the domestic life of old Jeju. Walk through traditional homes built with volcanic stone, observe harubang—the well-known stone statues that dot the island—and examine lava walls that shaped settlement patterns for centuries. The village offers an unfiltered view of how Jeju residents organized their homes, worked their land, and structured daily life before modernization.

From there, make your way to Seongsan Sunrise Peak (Seongsan Ilchulbong), a UNESCO World Heritage Site that rises dramatically from the coastal plain. The hike covers 1–2 kilometers on a well-maintained trail suitable for all fitness levels. As you ascend the volcanic pathways, you'll learn that this peak formed roughly 5,000 years ago during an underwater volcanic eruption—a geological event that created one of Jeju's most distinctive landmarks. The views from the summit extend across the island's volcanic terrain and out toward the sea, making the modest effort entirely worthwhile.

In the afternoon, transition to Hamdeok Beach. Here you have flexibility: spend time on the white sand and in the turquoise water, or take a shorter walk along the Olle Trail, the famous 437-kilometer loop hiking network that circumnavigates Jeju's perimeter. The Olle sections are well-marked and offer coastal perspectives that complement the morning's interior exploration.

As evening approaches, gather for the haenyeo performance—arguably the day's centerpiece. Haenyeo are Jeju's female divers, a tradition spanning centuries. Watch these women, some well into their 80s, descend into the sea and hold their breath for extended periods while harvesting abalone, conch, sea cucumbers, and other seafood. Their technique is both meditative and physically demanding, elegant through generations. After the performance concludes, you'll have time to interact directly with the divers—ask questions, observe their catch up close, and if inclined, purchase fresh seafood directly from them.

Finally, your guide will lead the group into downtown Jeju for the evening. This is your Big Night Out—a chance to celebrate with new friends and reflect on the day's experiences. Karaoke venues dot the area; local beer and fresh juice are both excellent options. Participation is entirely optional: some may prefer quieter reflection at a café or early rest before the next day's adventures. Either way, the evening belongs to the group to share as you wish.

Day 9 — Jeju Island: Your Choice of Exploration
This full day is yours to spend however you wish, with plenty of compelling options across the island. Whether you prefer active adventure, cultural immersion, or simple relaxation, Jeju offers something for every traveler.

Beach lovers should consider Geumneung Beach or Hyeopjae Beach, both offering peaceful settings to unwind and take in the island's coastline. If you're seeking more active pursuits, the Olle Trail presents an excellent opportunity. This 437 km loop circumnavigates the island's edge, featuring nature walks, cultural sites, waterfalls, and spectacular coastal views. Routes 6 and 7 are among the most popular sections. Your CEO can advise on logistics for reaching trailheads and can help you plan either a half-day or full-day hike suited to your fitness level.

For those interested in volcanic geology, the oreums—small dormant volcanic cones scattered across Jeju—offer accessible hiking with rewarding rewards. Seongsan Ilchulbong and Darangshi Oreum are particularly popular, with trails ranging from easy to moderate difficulty. The hikes showcase lush vegetation and diverse wildlife while providing commanding views across the island's landscape.

Culturally minded visitors should visit Bunker des Lumières, an immersive art exhibition housed in a former bunker in Jeju-si. The space uses advanced projection technology to display famous artworks across the bunker's interior walls, creating a mesmerizing experience as lively, moving images of masterpieces surround you as you walk through. The exhibition rotates its themes regularly, offering fresh perspectives with each visit.

Alternatively, you might spend time exploring Jeju City itself, wandering its neighborhoods and discovering local cafes, shops, and street-level culture at your own pace.

Your CEO has additional suggestions and can help with transportation logistics to reach various sections of the island, whether you're heading to a specific trailhead, beach, or attraction. The key is to take the day at your own rhythm and experience Jeju in whatever way appeals to you most.

Day 10 — Departure from Jeju
Depart at any time. Your guide can assist with onward travel arrangements or suggestions for extending your stay on Jeju or elsewhere in South Korea.

page.subtitle: Coconut plantations, Sigiriya, Kandy temples, elephant interactions, and Maldivian atolls across two weeks
page.summary: This 14-day journey moves between Sri Lanka's cultural and wildlife zones and concludes with time in the Maldives. The first nine days cover the western and central regions: coconut-plantation stays near Chilaw, cycling through farming villages to Sigiriya, exploration of Polonnaruwa's medieval ruins, visits to Kandy's Temple of Tooth Relic and surrounding hill-country villages, and a morning spent bathing an elephant in a river before the flight south. The final five days are spent island-based in the Maldives, with beach and water time. Transport throughout is by private vehicle with English-speaking driver; local guides lead excursions in each region. The itinerary is structured for families with children age six and older.

These animals, extinct in the wild since 1954, were reintroduced to Mongolia in the early 1990s through an international restoration effort led by Dutch conservationists. A day visit pairs the two-hour drive from the capital with morning or late-afternoon observation of the horses as they gather near streams, plus a briefing at the park's information center on the species and local wildlife.

The itinerary pairs guided hikes through protected forest reserves with cultural exchanges led by Indigenous hosts, visits to local woodworking studios, and opportunities to understand Paiwan religious practice and cuisine. page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Kaohsiung to Tjuvecekadan: Indigenous Village Tour and Community Meal
Private pickup occurs at Zuoying High Speed Rail Station. A guided hike leads to Tjuvecekadan, a Paiwan settlement roughly 50 minutes from the station, where a Paiwan host conducts a walking tour of the village's slate-stone architecture and settlement layout. A meal is served within the community. A hands-on activity follows before transfer to the evening's accommodation in Fangliao, where the first night is spent at a hot spring hotel.

Day 2 — Jinshuiying National Trail: 16 Kilometers Across Three Forest Reserves to the East Coast
The day is spent hiking Jinshuiying National Trail, a 16-kilometer route through three protected forest reserves. The trail passes suspension bridges and descends toward Taiwan's East Coast. Wildlife includes deer, monkeys, and pangolins; endemic and endangered orchid species grow along the route. Transfer follows to Taitung and check-in at a Zhiben hot spring hotel for the evening.

Day 3 — Taitung and Zhiben: Paiwan Culture, Woodcarving, and Forest Access
A local Indigenous guide leads a cultural tour focused on Paiwan religious practice and traditional food preparation. A visit to a local woodcarving studio follows. The group also visits the first Christian church in Taitung, which incorporates Paiwan cultural symbols into its design. The afternoon remains unstructured, allowing time to visit Zhiben National Forest or relax in the hotel's hot spring facilities before dinner.

Day 4 — Alangyi Historic Trail: Coastal Hike Along Southern Taiwan's Undeveloped Shoreline
The Alangyi Historic Trail traverses one of Taiwan's least-developed coastal sections. An Indigenous guide leads the group through the route's terrain and points of historical reference. Following the hike, transfer occurs to Mudan and a third hot spring hotel for evening rest.

Day 5 — Mudan: Shimen Battlefield, Abandoned Village, and Return to Kaohsiung
The morning begins with a visit to Shimen Battlefield, a site of documented conflict between Indigenous groups and Japanese forces. A hike follows to a nearby abandoned settlement with historical ties to early settlement patterns in the region. A final meal takes place in Mudan before private transfer returns the group to Zuoying High Speed Rail Station.

page.name: Kerala: Waterfalls, Backwaters & Beaches — 9 Days
page.subtitle: From Athirapally's waterfalls through Kumarakom's backwaters to the Arabian Sea coast, with nights aboard a traditional houseboat.
page.summary: This nine-day itinerary moves through Kerala's three primary landscape zones: the forested highlands of Athirapally, the lagoon systems of Kumarakom and Alleppey, and the Arabian Sea beaches of Marari. The route traces a south-westward path from Kochi through waterfalls and tea country, descends into the backwater region where traditional houseboats still operate as accommodation, and concludes on a palm-lined coast. The journey alternates between resort-based stays and a night aboard a kettuvallam—a wooden houseboat with cabin and deck—allowing travellers to move through the same waters that have defined Kerala's trade and settlement patterns for centuries. Most days include optional activities; several nights emphasize stillness and water-based movement rather than structured excursions.

Houseboat cruise through narrow backwater canals between Kumarakom and Alleppey

page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Kochi
Arrival at Kochi airport is followed by transfer to the hotel. The afternoon allows time to visit the old spice market district and the commercial streets of M.G. Road. The evening typically includes a sunset cruise on the backwaters and a screening of Kathakali, the classical dance-drama form native to Kerala, performed in traditional costume and makeup.

Day 2 — Kochi to Athirapally Waterfall
A two-hour drive inland (78 kilometers) leads to Athirapally, a settlement at the edge of the Sholayar forest range. The primary feature is the Athirapally Waterfall—an 80-foot drop often compared to Niagara Falls in scale—which flows year-round from a catchment in the surrounding hills. Check-in occurs at the hotel; the remainder of the day is unstructured.

Day 3 — Athirapally Forests and Falls
The day encompasses visits to Thumpurmuzhi Gardens and the Vazhachal and Charpa waterfalls, both within the same forest system as Athirapally. River fishing and visits to nearby tribal settlements are available as optional activities.

Day 4 — Athirapally to Kumarakom
A four-hour drive south (150 kilometers) descends from the forested highlands into the Kuttanad region and the Vembanad Lake system. Kumarakom sits on the lake's banks and serves as the base for the backwater portion of the itinerary. Resort accommodation is situated on the water's edge, surrounded by lagoon and narrow canals lined with coconut palms. The afternoon and evening allow for optional water sports and Ayurvedic massage treatments at the resort.

Day 5 — Kumarakom Backwaters
A day at the resort, with optional water sports and Ayurvedic massage available.

Day 6 — Houseboat Cruise Through Backwaters
A kettuvallam—a traditional wooden houseboat with cabin, sitting deck, and onboard cooking facilities—departs from the resort at a predetermined time. The vessel follows narrow canals linking Kumarakom to Alleppey, passing through a landscape of lagoons, coconut groves, and fishing settlements. The houseboat serves as both transport and overnight accommodation, allowing travellers to move slowly through the backwater system without daily transfers. A full night is spent aboard.

Day 7 — Alleppey to Marari Beach
After breakfast on the houseboat, a 35-minute drive (22 kilometers) leads to Marari, a beach village on the Arabian Sea coast south of Alleppey. Check-in occurs at a beach resort. A walking tour of the resort's shoreline is typically offered in the late morning or afternoon.

Day 8 — Marari Beach
Morning visits to a fisherman village adjacent to the resort provide a view of local fishing practices and daily life along the coast. Water sports and Ayurvedic treatments remain available at the resort throughout the day.

Day 9 — Marari to Kochi Departure
After breakfast, you'll check out from the resort and transfer to Kochi airport for your onward journey. The drive north covers 58 kilometers and takes approximately one hour, marking the end of your Kerala tour.

page.summary: This eight-day itinerary pairs coastal relaxation on Sri Lanka's northeast coast with a safari-based wildlife experience in Wilpattu National Park. The route begins in Trincomalee, where the Indian Ocean provides opportunities for snorkeling and diving among coral ecosystems, followed by a transition into the dry-zone jungle of Wilpattu, home to Sri Lankan elephants, leopards, sloth bears, and substantial populations of resident and migratory waterbirds. The journey concludes with a night in Negombo before departure. Accommodation ranges from beachside property to safari camp tents, with transfers by private vehicle throughout.

page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Colombo & Transfer to Trincomalee
Arrival at Colombo International Airport. A driver meets guests in the arrivals lounge for a six-hour transfer to Trincomalee on Sri Lanka's northeast coast. The route traverses inland terrain before reaching the Indian Ocean. Evening check-in at Jungle Beach in Kuchchuweli, a beachside property set among tropical vegetation.

Day 2 — Trincomalee Beach Rest
A full day at Jungle Beach. The property sits directly on the coast, with the hotel's architecture incorporating existing trees and plant life into its structure. Guests spend the day at leisure on the beach or within the resort grounds. Overnight at Jungle Beach.

Day 3 — Pigeon Island Reef Snorkeling & Diving
An excursion to Pigeon Island, a protected marine reserve offshore from Trincomalee. The coral ecosystem supports over 100 species of tropical corals and approximately 300 species of reef fish, along with Black Tip reef sharks, rays, and sea turtles. Snorkeling and diving options allow direct observation of the underwater habitat. Return to Jungle Beach for overnight.

Day 4 — Trincomalee Beach Rest
Another leisure day at Jungle Beach. Overnight at the resort.

Day 5 — Transfer to Wilpattu National Park & First Safari
A two-hour transfer by private vehicle westward to Wilpattu National Park, Sri Lanka's largest terrestrial protected area. Guests arrive at the park entrance at noon and are driven to the safari campsite. Wilpattu's dry-zone jungle landscape is densely vegetated and dotted with approximately 30 natural freshwater lakes (locally called villus), which sustain populations of resident and migratory waterfowl including garganey, pintail, whistling teal, spoonbill, white ibis, large white egret, cattle egret, and purple heron. The park also hosts gull, tern, owl, kite, and eagle species, plus endemic species such as the Sri Lanka jungle fowl, little cormorant, and painted stork. Mammal species found in the park include Sri Lankan elephant, Sri Lankan leopard, sloth bear, spotted deer, buffalo, sambar, and mongoose. A late afternoon game drive and dinner precede overnight in a safari camp tent.

Day 6 — Wilpattu Safari and Campsite Days
Early morning and evening game drives search for large mammals and waterbirds. Mid-day at leisure in camp. Overnight at the safari campsite.

Day 7 — Wilpattu Morning Drive & Transfer to Negombo
Early morning game drive, then breakfast at the campsite. A three-hour drive brings you to Suriya Resort in Waikkal for the night.

Day 8 — Departure
Breakfast at Suriya Resort. A thirty-minute drive to Colombo International Airport for departure.

page.summary: This seven-day itinerary moves through Sri Lanka's primary wildlife reserves, beginning in the montane forests of Kitulgala and progressing through the lowland parks of Udawalawe, Bundala, and Yala. The route centers on morning and evening safari drives and bird-watching walks, timed to coincide with peak animal activity. Kitulgala's forest trails yield endemic species—Orange-billed Babblers, Chestnut-backed Owlets, Green Pit Vipers—and a diversity of butterflies and reptiles. Udawalawe's open grassland and reservoir support a permanent population of approximately 250 Sri Lankan elephants, among the easiest on the island to observe. Bundala's wetlands attract around 100 water bird species, including seasonal Greater Flamingos in flocks exceeding 1,000 birds, alongside resident Lesser Whistling Ducks, Little Cormorants, and waders. Yala, the largest reserve, holds all four members of Sri Lanka's 'big four' wildlife: elephant herds, sloth bears, leopards (elusive and primarily nocturnal), and wild buffalo. Transfers between parks involve three to four-hour drives; accommodation is provided in safari lodges positioned near park gates. All meals, park entrance fees, and English-speaking guide services are included.

page.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Colombo and Transfer to Kitulgala
Meet your representative at Colombo International Airport and transfer to Kitulgala, a 2-hour drive inland. An evening bird-watching trail visits the village surroundings. Overnight at Kitulgala Adventures.

Day 2 — Kitulgala Bird Watching and Forest Wildlife
Start early with a bird-watching trail through Kitulgala's forests, a destination prized by nature enthusiasts for its concentration of endemic species. The region consistently yields sightings of Sri Lanka Orange-billed Babblers and Chestnut-backed Owlets, along with reptiles including Green Pit Vipers and Earless Lizards. A variety of butterfly species inhabit the trails as well. After breakfast at the camp site, spend the rest of the day at leisure or exploring the immediate surroundings. An evening bird-watching walk in the village provides another opportunity to observe local wildlife as light conditions shift. Return to Kitulgala Adventures for the night.

Day 3 — Udawalawe National Park Safari
After breakfast, a transfer takes you south to Udawalawe National Park, a reserve centered on its reservoir and surrounding grassland. The landscape here favors wildlife viewing across open terrain. You'll visit the park on an evening safari drive, searching for elephants, buffalo, and other inhabitants as light begins to soften. The day concludes at Nil Diya Mankada Safari Lodge.

Day 4 — Udawalawe Elephants to Bundala's Waterbirds
Begin with a morning safari at Udawalawe National Park, where Sri Lankan elephants congregate around the reservoir. The park's open habitats make these animals relatively easy to locate—roughly 250 are permanently resident here. The elephants' attraction to the water creates reliable sighting opportunities across the landscape.

Mid-morning, transfer south to Bundala National Park, a coastal wetland system of lagoons and shallow waters. An evening safari follows, focusing on Bundala's avian wealth. The park hosts approximately 100 bird species, with half being seasonal migrants. Greater Flamingos from India's Rann of Kutch arrive in massive flocks exceeding 1,000 individuals, though their numbers fluctuate seasonally. Year-round residents include Lesser Whistling Ducks, Garganey, Little Cormorants, Indian Cormorants, Grey Herons, Black-headed Ibises, Eurasian Spoonbills, Asian Openbills, and Painted Storks. Medium and small wading species of Tringa and Charadrius subspecies are common. Rarer sightings include Black-necked Storks, Lesser Adjutants, and Eurasian Coots. Overnight stay at Yala Lake Camp.

Day 5 — Full-Day Safari in Yala National Park
A full-day safari in Yala National Park covers the island's largest wildlife reserve and its primary habitat for all four members of Sri Lanka's 'big four': elephants, sloth bears, leopards, and wild buffalo. Elephant herds move seasonally to smaller reservoirs—Butuwe and Mahaseelawa—during the dry season, where they congregate and are readily visible. Uraniya reservoir is known for aquatic birds, wild buffalo, and both Mugger and saltwater crocodiles. Sloth bears, solitary and primarily nocturnal, are harder to encounter; sightings are seasonal. Leopards remain elusive, requiring persistence and luck. The reserve spans varied terrain, and safaris follow established routes through grassland and scattered woodland. Overnight stay at Yala Lake Camp.

Day 6 — Tissamaharama Bird Walk and Return to Colombo
A morning bird-watching walk covers the forest and reservoir system at Tissamaharama, near Yala's boundary. After breakfast, the journey north begins with a transfer back to Colombo by road. Overnight accommodation is at Cinnamon Red hotel in the capital.

Day 7 — Departure
After breakfast, transfer to Colombo International Airport for departure, approximately 1 hour from the hotel.

Day 1  Seoul
Welcome to Seoul! As fellow travellers are arriving throughout the day, there are no planned activities until a group meeting at 6 pm. Check into the hotel and enjoy the city.

After the welcome meeting, join your CEO for an orientation walk down Cheonggyecheon Stream to learn about Seoul while walking past small waterfalls and nearly two dozen overhead bridges. Then, enjoy the dense grid of streets found in the bustling neighbourhood of Myeongdong which is packed with people at all hours of the day looking to enjoy some of the best shopping, street food, and nightlife in all of Korea.

Opt for a group dinner to end your first night!

The most convenient way to get around South Korea is by public transportation and on foot. The country's train system is world renowned so the majority of our trips utilize this efficient train network. In this tour, you will need to be able to spend the majority of the day on your feet and carry your luggage through busy train stations and streets. Please ensure you are fit enough to carry your own luggage and spend most of the day on your feet.

Seoul Orientation Walk                           Seoul
Enjoy a brief walk with your CEO who will give you some tips on finding things like supermarkets, main squares, and ATMs. You'll be taken through Cheonggyecheon Stream which is an 8.4 kilometre (5.2 mile) waterway and public space that runs through the heart of downtown Seoul. Myeongdong is another popular spot you'll hit on your orientation walk. This exciting district features street food carts, major shopping malls, and entertainment.

Your Welcome Moment: Meet Your CEO and Group
Your opportunity to meet your CEO and fellow travellers, and learn more about your tour. Opt to join the group for a local meal afterwards. Don't forget to see the notice in the lobby (or ask reception) for the official time and place to meet up with the group.

After exploring the city, opt to see a show, explore a local museum, or hit the pavement and eat your way through street markets trying local fares such as bibimbap, soondae, and kimchi.

Gyeongbokgung Palace                          Seoul
Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace, the main royal palace of the Joseon Dynasty built in 1395. The palace has been destroyed many times over, but more than 50 per cent of the buildings are still standing or are restored. The complex is also home to the National Palace Museum and the National Folk Museum.

Insadong Alley                                         Seoul
Explore the narrow and hidden alleys of one of the most memorable places in Seoul. Now filled with antique shops, galleries, tea houses and traditional restaurants, this area once housed the royal studio for painters during the Joseon Dynasty.

National Folklore Museum                       Seoul
Located within the grounds of the Gyeongbokgung Palace, learn about the history and traditions of the Korean people during the Joseon era.

Be transported back 600 years into Seoul's past while walking through Bukchon Hanok Village, which boasts the largest cluster of privately owned traditional Korean wooden homes (hanok) in Seoul. Keep an eye out for the half-dozen or so alleys that have beautifully restored architectural features like small courtyards, decorative outer walls, and dark tiled roofs.

Optional Activities - Day 2

Gwangjang Market Visit                           Seoul
Gwangjang Market is one of the oldest and largest traditional markets in South Korea, with more than 5,000 shops. Famous for its fabric, local treasures, and noted to be one of the best places to go for authentic Korean street food in Seoul, you don't want to miss Gwangjang Market.

Really get to know Seoul with a stop at the Seoul Museum of History, which highlights each segment of the city's past from the Stone Age to present day. Discover one of the museum's recent creations – a large floor map of Seoul, great for plotting out your next steps!

During the stay the group will learn about temple etiquette, watch a monk martial arts performance, experience the daily prayer ritual and a temple style dinner.

Stay in rooms called Ondol. These rooms are very traditional, heated to be cozy and comfortable, with beds made up directly on the floor. The rooms here are multi-share, divided up by male and female rooms. Enjoy a traditional dinner and breakfast during the stay.

Cheomseongdae was used for observing the stars in order to forecast the weather in the ancient scientific hub of Gyeongju.

The complex is beautiful with its rolling mounds and gardens, but the real treat can be found inside the tombs, the most famous being Cheonmachong and Hwangnamdaechong. Each tomb holds thousands of relics that gives us a window into the Silla Dynasty and its royal family. The contents of these tombs are over 1,500 years old and a great treasure to anyone who enjoys Korean history and artistic beauty.

After arriving in Seoul by train, check out Korea's oldest traditional market - Namdaemun Market. page.name: South Korea: Palace, Temple & Island — 13 Days
page.subtitle: Seoul to Jeju via high-speed rail, mountain temples, DMZ, and volcanic coastline
page.summary: This 13-day itinerary moves systematically through South Korea's layered geography and history: Seoul's palace grounds and street markets, a night in a working Buddhist temple in Gyeongju, the DMZ's heavily militarized border, hanok villages in Jeonju, bamboo forests and tea fields in the southwest, and three days on Jeju Island exploring waterfalls, lava formations, and the haenyeo women divers. Travel is by high-speed train, private vehicle, and domestic flight. Most days involve substantial walking and navigation through busy transit hubs; pack accordingly.

Visit the Korean Demilitarized Zone, a 4-kilometre buffer spanning 250 kilometres between North and South Korea
Stroll through Damyang Bamboo Forest, South Korea's largest bamboo grove at 150,000 square metres
Watch haenyeo women divers harvest seafood from the sea using breath-hold techniques on Jeju Island
Hike Seongsan Sunrise Peak, a UNESCO World Heritage volcanic formation on Jeju created 5,000 years ago
Visit Yangdong Folk Village, a 500-year-old UNESCO site with over 160 traditionally preserved homes
